translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 122.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 122.

sentences.zh: 【宋紀四】 起重光協洽，盡旃蒙大淵獻，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Song Annals 4] From Chongguang Xieqia through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Annals 4] From Chongguang Xieqia through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之下元嘉八年（

translations.literal: The lower part of "Emperor Wen of the Ancestor [dynasty], Part One" — Yuanjia year 8 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, Part One (continued) — Yuanjia year 8 (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元四三一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, corresponding to 431 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, corresponding to 431 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午朔，燕大赦，改元大興。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (renwu), Yan proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (renwu), Northern Yan proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Daxing.

sentences.zh: 丙申，檀道道濟等自清水救滑台，魏叔孫建、長孫道生拒之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tan Daoji and others set out from Qingshui to relieve Huating; the Wei generals Shusun Jian and Zhangsun Daosheng barred their way.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Tan Daoji and others marched from Qingshui to relieve Huating, while the Northern Wei generals Shusun Jian and Zhangsun Daosheng blocked them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，道濟至壽張，遇魏安平公乙謝眷，道濟帥寧塑將軍王仲德、驍騎將軍段宏奮擊，大破之；

translations.literal: On dingyou, Daoji reached Shouzhang and encountered the Wei Prince of Anping, Yixie Juan. Daoji led the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Wang Zhongde and the General of Valiant Cavalry Duan Hong in a fierce attack and routed them utterly;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Daoji reached Shouzhang and met the Northern Wei Prince of Anping, Yixie Juan. Leading Generals Wang Zhongde and Duan Hong, he struck hard and won a crushing victory;

sentences.zh: 轉戰至高梁亭，斬魏濟州刺史悉煩庫結。

translations.literal: fighting on to Gaoliangting, where he beheaded the Wei Inspector of Jizhou, Xifan Kujie.
translations.idiomatic: then fought through to Gaoliangting, where he killed the Northern Wei inspector of Jizhou, Xifan Kujie.

sentences.zh: 夏主擊秦將姚獻，敗之；

translations.literal: The Xia ruler attacked the Qin general Yao Xian and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler attacked the Western Qin general Yao Xian and defeated him;

sentences.zh: 遂遣其叔父北平公韋伐帥眾一萬攻南安。

translations.literal: then sent his uncle, the Prince of Beiping Wei Fa, to lead ten thousand men in an attack on Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his uncle, the Prince of Beiping Wei Fa, at the head of ten thousand troops to besiege Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 城中大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: Within the city there was severe famine, and men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the city, and people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 秦侍中、征虜將軍出連輔政，侍中、右衛將軍乞伏延祚，吏部尚書乞伏跋跋，逾城奔夏；

translations.literal: The Qin Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Chilian Fuzheng, the Palace Attendant and General of the Right Guard Qifu Yanzuo, and the Minister of Personnel Qifu Baba, fled over the wall to Xia;
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin's Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Chilian Fuzheng, Palace Attendant and General of the Right Guard Qifu Yanzuo, and Minister of Personnel Qifu Baba, fled over the walls to Xia;

sentences.zh: 秦王暮末窮蹙，輿櫬出降，並沮渠興國送於上邽。

translations.literal: the Qin king Mumo, in desperate straits, came out bearing his coffin to surrender, and he and Juqu Xingguo were sent to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: the Western Qin king Mumo, brought to bay, came out with a coffin on a carriage to surrender; he and Juqu Xingguo were sent to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 秦太子司直焦楷奔廣寧，泣謂其父遺曰：「大人荷國寵靈，居籓鎮重任。

translations.literal: The Qin crown prince's Director of Justice Jiao Kai fled to Guangning and, weeping, said to his father Yi: "Father, you have received the state's favor and grace and hold a weighty post as frontier commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Kai, Director of Justice to the Western Qin crown prince, fled to Guangning and wept as he told his father Yi, "Father, the state has heaped honor upon you and entrusted you with a great frontier command.

sentences.zh: 今本朝顛覆，豈得不率見眾唱大義以殄寇仇！」

translations.literal: Now that our dynasty has been overthrown, how can you fail to lead the men before you in proclaiming the righteous cause and destroying the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty lies in ruins—how can you refuse to rally the troops at hand, raise the banner of righteousness, and destroy the foe?"

sentences.zh: 遺曰：「今主上已陷賊庭，吾非愛死而忘義，顧以大兵追之，是趣絕其命也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The sovereign is already in the enemy's hands. It is not that I love life and forget duty; but if we pursue with a large force, we will only hasten his death.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Our lord is already in enemy hands. It is not that I cling to life and forget my duty—but if we chase them with a large army, we will only hasten his end.

sentences.zh: 不如擇王族之賢者，奉以為主而伐之，庶有濟也。」

translations.literal: Better to choose a worthy man of the royal house, set him up as ruler, and attack them—then there may be hope of success."
translations.idiomatic: Better to choose a worthy prince of the royal house, set him up as ruler, and march against the enemy—that way we may yet prevail."

sentences.zh: 楷乃築誓眾，二旬之間，赴者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Kai then raised an oath-altar and rallied the people; within twenty days more than ten thousand came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then raised an oath-altar and rallied the people; within twenty days more than ten thousand men had gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 會遺病卒，楷不能獨舉事，亡奔河西。

translations.literal: Just then Yi died of illness, and Kai could not act alone; he fled to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: But Yi fell ill and died, and Kai could not carry the enterprise alone; he fled west to the Hexi corridor.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，以尚書右僕射江夷為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuwu, Jiang Yi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuwu, Jiang Yi was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟等進至濟上，二十餘日間，前後與魏三十餘戰，道濟多捷。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and the others advanced to the Ji River. Over more than twenty days they fought the Wei more than thirty times in all, and Daoji won most of the engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and his forces advanced to the Ji River. Over more than twenty days they fought the Northern Wei more than thirty times, and Daoji won most of the battles.

sentences.zh: 軍至歷城，叔孫建等縱輕騎邀其前後，焚燒谷草。

translations.literal: When the army reached Licheng, Shusun Jian and the others sent light cavalry to harass them front and rear and burned the grain and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Licheng, Shusun Jian and others sent light cavalry to harry them from front and rear and burned the grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 道濟軍乏食，不能進。

translations.literal: Daoji's army lacked food and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's army ran short of food and could advance no farther.

sentences.zh: 由是安頡、司馬楚之等得專力攻滑台，魏主復使楚兵將軍王慧龍助之。

translations.literal: Thereby An Li and Sima Chuzhi and the others were able to concentrate on attacking Huating; the Wei ruler again sent the Chu-Bing General Wang Huilong to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: This allowed An Li, Sima Chuzhi, and the others to concentrate on the siege of Huating, and the Northern Wei emperor again sent the Chu-Bing General Wang Huilong to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 朱修之堅守數月，糧盡，與士卒熏鼠食之。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi held firm for several months; when grain was exhausted, he and his soldiers smoked rats and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi held out for months; when provisions ran out, he and his men smoked rats and ate them.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏克滑台，執修之及東郡太守申謨，虜獲萬餘人。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wei captured Huating, seized Xiuzhi and the Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo, and took more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Northern Wei took Huating, captured Xiuzhi and the Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo, and seized more than ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 謨，鐘之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Mo was a great-grandson of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was a great-grandson of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏主還平城，大饗，告廟，將帥及百官皆受賞，戰士賜覆十年。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng, held a great feast, reported to the ancestral temple, and rewarded generals and officials alike; the soldiers were granted ten years' worth of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng, held a great feast, reported victory to the ancestral temple, and rewarded generals and officials; common soldiers received ten years' worth of clothing.

sentences.zh: 於是魏南鄙大水，民多餓死。

translations.literal: Thereupon the southern marches of Wei suffered great floods, and many of the people starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile great floods struck the southern frontier of Northern Wei, and many people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉絜言於魏主曰：「自頃邊寇內侵，戎車屢駕；

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Jie said to the Wei ruler: "Of late border enemies have invaded within, and the war-chariots have been driven out again and again;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Jie said to the Northern Wei emperor, "In recent times border enemies have invaded our lands, and the war-chariots have been sent out again and again;

sentences.zh: 天贊聖明，所在克殄；

translations.literal: Heaven has aided Your Sacred Sagacity, and wherever you go the enemy is destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has aided Your Sacred Sagacity, and wherever you march the enemy is destroyed;

sentences.zh: 方難既平，皆蒙優錫。

translations.literal: now that the troubles in every quarter have been pacified, all have received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: now that troubles on every front have been pacified, all have received generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 而郡國之民，雖不征討，服勤農桑，以供軍國，實經世之大本，府庫之所資。

translations.literal: Yet the people of the commanderies and kingdoms, though they do not go on campaign, labor diligently at farming and sericulture to supply the army and the state—this is truly the great foundation of governing the age and the source of the treasury's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people of the commanderies and kingdoms, though they do not go to war, labor at farming and sericulture to supply army and state—this is the great foundation of governance and the treasury's lifeblood.

sentences.zh: 今自山以東，遍遭水害，應加哀矜，以弘覆育。」

translations.literal: Now from the mountains eastward they have everywhere suffered flood damage; they should be shown added compassion and pity, to extend Your nurturing care."
translations.idiomatic: Now from the mountains eastward they have suffered flood damage everywhere; they deserve added compassion and relief, to extend Your nurturing care."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之，復境內一歲租賦。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler assented and remitted one year's land tax and levies throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and remitted one year's land tax and levies throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟等食盡，自歷城引還；

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and the others, their food exhausted, withdrew from Licheng;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and his men, their provisions exhausted, withdrew from Licheng;

sentences.zh: 軍士有亡降魏者，具告之。

translations.literal: some soldiers deserted to Wei and told them everything in detail.
translations.idiomatic: some soldiers deserted to the Northern Wei and told them everything.

sentences.zh: 魏人追之，眾恟懼，將潰。

translations.literal: The Wei pursued them; the troops were alarmed and on the verge of breaking.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei pursued them; the troops panicked and were on the verge of breaking.

sentences.zh: 道濟夜唱籌量沙，以所餘少米覆其上。

translations.literal: Daoji had them count out sand by night with measuring sticks and spread the little rice that remained on top.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji had his men measure out sand by night with counting sticks and spread the little rice that remained on top.

sentences.zh: 及旦，魏軍見之，謂道濟資糧有餘，以降者為妄而斬之。

translations.literal: At dawn the Wei army saw this and believed Daoji still had ample provisions; they regarded the deserters as lying and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Northern Wei troops saw this and believed Daoji still had ample provisions; they took the deserters for liars and executed them.

sentences.zh: 時道濟兵少，魏兵甚盛，騎士四合。

translations.literal: At that time Daoji had few troops while the Wei forces were very strong, with horsemen closing in on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's force was small while the Northern Wei army was very strong, with horsemen closing in on every side.

sentences.zh: 道濟命軍士皆被甲，己白服乘輿，引兵徐出。

translations.literal: Daoji ordered all the soldiers to don armor; he himself wore white robes and rode in a carriage, leading the army out slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji ordered every soldier into armor; he himself wore white robes and rode in an open carriage, leading the army out at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 魏人以為有伏兵，不敢逼，稍稍引退，道濟全軍而返。

translations.literal: The Wei thought there were ambush troops and did not dare press close; they gradually drew back, and Daoji brought the whole army back safely.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei believed ambush troops lay in wait and did not dare press close; they gradually withdrew, and Daoji brought his entire army home safely.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭思話聞道濟南歸，欲委鎮保險，濟南太守蕭承之固諫，不從。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Qingzhou Xiao Sihua, hearing that Daoji had returned south, wished to abandon his post and hold a defensible position; the Administrator of Jinan Xiao Chengzhi strongly remonstrated, but Sihua would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Qingzhou, hearing that Daoji had returned south, wished to abandon his post and fall back to safer ground; Xiao Chengzhi, Administrator of Jinan, urged him strongly not to, but Sihua would not listen.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，思話棄鎮奔平昌；

translations.literal: On dingchou, Sihua abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Sihua abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang;

sentences.zh: 參軍劉振之戍下邳，聞之，亦委城走。

translations.literal: the staff officer Liu Zhenzhi, garrisoning Xiapi, heard of this and also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenzhi, a staff officer garrisoning Xiapi, heard of this and abandoned the city as well.

sentences.zh: 魏軍竟不至，而東陽積聚已為百姓所焚。

translations.literal: The Wei army never came, but the stores accumulated at Dongyang had already been burned by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei army never came, but the stores at Dongyang had already been burned by local people.

sentences.zh: 思話坐征，系尚方。

translations.literal: Sihua was summoned to account and imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua was summoned to the capital for trial and held in the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 燕王立夫人慕容氏為王后。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler installed Lady Murong as queen.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Northern Yan installed Lady Murong as queen.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏安頡等還平城。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Wei generals An Li and others returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, An Li and the other Northern Wei generals returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏主嘉朱修之守節，拜侍中，妻以宗女。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler praised Zhu Xiuzhi's steadfast loyalty, appointed him Palace Attendant, and gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor praised Zhu Xiuzhi's steadfast loyalty, made him Palace Attendant, and gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage.

sentences.zh: 初，帝之遣到彥之也，戒之曰：「若北國兵動，先其未至，逕前入河；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor sent Dao Yanzhi, he admonished him: "If the northern state moves its troops, before they arrive go straight forward into the Yellow River;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor sent Dao Yanzhi north, he instructed him: "If the northern state moves its troops, before they arrive march straight into the Yellow River region;

sentences.zh: 若其不動，留彭城勿進。」

translations.literal: if they do not move, remain at Pengcheng and do not advance."
translations.idiomatic: if they do not move, hold Pengcheng and do not advance."

sentences.zh: 及安頡得宋俘，魏主始聞其言。

translations.literal: When An Li captured Song prisoners, the Wei ruler first heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: When An Li captured Song prisoners, the Northern Wei emperor first heard these instructions.

sentences.zh: 謂公卿曰：「卿輩前謂我用崔浩計為謬，驚怖固諫。

translations.literal: He said to the dukes and ministers: "You all formerly said that my use of Cui Hao's plan was mistaken and remonstrated in alarm and fear.
translations.idiomatic: He told the dukes and ministers, "You all said my adoption of Cui Hao's plan was mistaken and remonstrated in alarm.

sentences.zh: 常勝之家，始皆自謂逾人，至於歸終，乃不能及。」

translations.literal: A household that always wins at first thinks itself superior to others; only when the game ends do they find they cannot match it."
translations.idiomatic: Those who always win begin by thinking themselves superior; only when the game ends do they find they cannot keep up."

sentences.zh: 司馬楚之上疏，以為諸方已平，請大舉伐宋，魏主以兵久勞，不許。

translations.literal: Sima Chuzhi submitted a memorial arguing that every quarter had been pacified and requesting a major campaign against Song; the Wei ruler, because the troops had long been wearied, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi submitted a memorial arguing that every front had been pacified and urging a major campaign against Song; the Northern Wei emperor, considering the troops long wearied, refused.

sentences.zh: 徽楚之為散騎常侍，以王慧龍為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: He recalled Chuzhi to be Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and appointed Wang Huilong Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Chuzhi to court as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and appointed Wang Huilong Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 慧龍在郡十年，農戰並修，大著聲績，歸附者萬餘家。

translations.literal: Huilong was in the commandery ten years, developing both agriculture and warfare; his reputation and achievements were great, and more than ten thousand households came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong governed the commandery for ten years, developing both farming and warfare; his reputation and achievements were great, and more than ten thousand households submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 帝縱反間於魏，云「慧龍自以功高位下，欲引宋人入寇，因執司馬楚之以叛。」

translations.literal: The Emperor spread disinformation in Wei, saying: "Huilong, thinking his merit great but his rank low, wishes to bring Song troops in to invade and will seize Sima Chuzhi as a pretext for rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor spread disinformation in Northern Wei, saying, "Huilong, believing his merit great but his rank low, means to invite Song troops to invade and will seize Sima Chuzhi as a pretext for rebellion."

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，賜慧龍璽書曰：「劉義隆畏將軍如虎，欲相中害，朕自知之。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler heard this, he sent Huilong an imperial letter with the seal, saying: "Liu Yilong fears you, General, as a tiger and wishes to harm you by slander—I know this myself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei emperor heard this, he sent Huilong an imperial letter bearing the seal: "Liu Yilong fears you, General, as he would a tiger and wishes to destroy you by slander—I know this myself.

sentences.zh: 風塵之言，想不足介意。」

translations.literal: Words borne on the wind and dust—I trust you will not take them to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors borne on the wind—I trust you will not take them to heart."

sentences.zh: 帝復遣客呂玄伯刺之，曰：「得慧龍首，封二百戶男，賞絹千匹。」

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent the agent Lü Xuanbo to assassinate him, saying: "Whoever obtains Huilong's head shall be enfeoffed as a baron of two hundred households and rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor again sent the agent Lü Xuanbo to assassinate him, promising, "Whoever brings me Huilong's head shall be enfeoffed as a baron of two hundred households and rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 玄伯詐為降人，求屏人有所論；

translations.literal: Xuanbo pretended to be a defector and asked to speak with Huilong alone;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo posed as a defector and asked for a private audience;

sentences.zh: 慧龍疑之，使人探其懷，得尺刀。

translations.literal: Huilong was suspicious and had someone search his bosom, finding a foot-long knife.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong grew suspicious and had someone search him, finding a foot-long knife.

sentences.zh: 玄伯叩頭請死，慧龍曰：「各為其主耳。」

translations.literal: Xuanbo kowtowed and begged for death. Huilong said: "Each man serves his own lord—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo kowtowed and begged for death. Huilong said, "Each man serves his own lord—that is all."

sentences.zh: 釋之。

translations.literal: He released him.
translations.idiomatic: He let him go.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「宋人為謀未已，不殺玄伯，無以制將來。」

translations.literal: Those at his side remonstrated: "The Song people's plots are not ended; if you do not kill Xuanbo, you cannot restrain those to come."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged, "The Song are not finished plotting; if you do not kill Xuanbo, you cannot deter those who come after."

sentences.zh: 慧龍曰：「死生有命，彼亦安能害我！

translations.literal: Huilong said: "Life and death are ordained by fate—how could they harm me!
translations.idiomatic: Huilong said, "Life and death are ordained by fate—how could they harm me!

sentences.zh: 我以仁義為扞蔽，又何憂乎！」

translations.literal: I take benevolence and righteousness as my shield—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: I take benevolence and righteousness as my shield—what is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 遂捨之。

translations.literal: He then let him go.
translations.idiomatic: And he let him go.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，庚寅，魏主如雲中。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on gengyin, the Wei ruler went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on gengyin, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 夏主殺乞伏暮末及其宗族五百人。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler killed Qifu Mumo and five hundred members of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler executed Qifu Mumo and five hundred members of his clan.

sentences.zh: 夏主畏魏人之逼，擁秦民十餘萬口，自治城濟河，欲擊河西王蒙遜而奪其地。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler, fearing pressure from the Wei, drove more than a hundred thousand Qin people from Zicheng across the river, intending to strike the King of Hexi Meng Xun and seize his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing pressure from the Northern Wei, the Xia ruler drove more than a hundred thousand Western Qin subjects from Zicheng across the river, intending to strike Meng Xun, King of Hexi, and seize his lands.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕瑰遣益州刺史慕利延、寧州刺史拾虔帥騎三萬，乘其半濟，邀擊之，執夏主定以歸，沮渠興國被創而死。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent the Inspector of Yizhou Murong Liyan and the Inspector of Ningzhou Shiqian to lead thirty thousand horsemen, struck while the Xia were half across the river, captured the Xia ruler Ding and brought him back; Juqu Xingguo was wounded and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent Inspectors Murong Liyan and Shiqian at the head of thirty thousand horsemen to strike while the Xia were half across the river; they captured the Xia ruler Ding and brought him back, and Juqu Xingguo died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 拾虔，樹洛干之子也。

translations.literal: Shiqian was a son of Shulogan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was a son of Shulogan.

sentences.zh: 魏之邊吏獲柔然邏者二十餘人，魏主賜衣服而遣之，柔然悅。

translations.literal: A Wei border official captured more than twenty Rouran scouts; the Wei ruler gave them clothing and sent them back, and the Rouran were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: A Northern Wei border official captured more than twenty Rouran scouts; the emperor gave them clothing and sent them back, and the Rouran were pleased.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙未，柔然敕連可汗遣使詣魏，魏主厚禮之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on yiwei, the Rouran Khan Chilelian sent envoys to Wei, and the Wei ruler treated them with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yiwei, the Rouran khan Chilelian sent envoys to Northern Wei, and the emperor received them with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣散騎侍郎周紹來聘，且求昏；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhou Shao on a friendly mission and also to request a marriage alliance;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor sent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhou Shao on a friendly mission and also to propose a marriage alliance;

sentences.zh: 帝依違答之。

translations.literal: the Emperor answered evasively.
translations.idiomatic: the Song emperor answered evasively.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史江夏王義恭，年寢長，欲專政事，長史劉湛每裁抑之，遂與湛有隙。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, as he grew older wished to monopolize government affairs; the Chief Administrator Liu Zhan constantly checked and restrained him, and thus a rift opened between them.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and Inspector of Jingzhou, grew older and wished to monopolize government affairs; his Chief Administrator Liu Zhan constantly checked and restrained him, and a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 帝心重湛，使人詰讓義恭，且和解之。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued Zhan in his heart, sent someone to rebuke Yigong, and also sought to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Zhan highly, sent someone to rebuke Yigong, and also sought to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 是時，王華、王曇首皆卒，領軍將軍殷景仁素與湛善，白帝以時賢零落，征湛為太子詹事，加給事中，共參政事。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou had both died; the General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren had long been on good terms with Zhan and told the Emperor that the worthies of the age were dwindling; Zhan was summoned as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with added appointment as Palace Attendant, to participate jointly in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou had both died by then; Yin Jingren, General of the Palace Guard, had long been friendly with Zhan and told the emperor that the worthies of the age were dwindling; Zhan was summoned as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with added appointment as Palace Attendant, to join in governing.

sentences.zh: 以雍州刺史張邵代湛為撫軍長史、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao, Inspector of Yongzhou, was appointed in Zhan's place as Chief Administrator of the Pacification Army and Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao, Inspector of Yongzhou, replaced Zhan as Chief Administrator of the Pacification Army and Colonel of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 頃之，邵坐在雍州營私畜聚，贓滿二百四十五萬，下廷尉，當死。

translations.literal: Before long, Shao was charged with enriching himself through private accumulation while in Yongzhou; the bribes totaled 2,450,000, and he was sent to the Minister of Justice, for which the penalty was death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shao was charged with amassing private wealth while in Yongzhou; the bribes totaled 2,450,000 cash units, and he was sent to the Minister of Justice, for which the penalty was death.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍謝述上表，陳邵先朝舊勳，蒙優貸。

translations.literal: The General of the Left Guard Xie Shu submitted a memorial stating that Shao was a meritorious minister of the former reign and should receive lenient treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shu, General of the Left Guard, submitted a memorial arguing that Shao was a meritorious minister of the former reign and deserved lenient treatment.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔酬納，免邵官，削爵土。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote a personal edict in reply accepting the proposal, removed Shao from office, and stripped his title and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a personal edict accepting the proposal, removed Shao from office, and stripped his title and fief.

sentences.zh: 述謂其子綜曰：「主上矜邵夙誠，特加曲恕，吾所言謬會，故特見酬納耳。

translations.literal: Shu said to his son Zong: "The sovereign, taking pity on Shao's long-standing loyalty, especially extended gracious pardon. What I said happened to accord with his wish, and so he especially accepted my proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Shu told his son Zong, "The sovereign, taking pity on Shao's long-standing loyalty, especially extended gracious pardon. What I said happened to accord with his wish, and so he especially accepted my proposal.

sentences.zh: 若此跡宣佈，則為侵奪主恩，不可之大者也。」

translations.literal: If this fact were made public, it would amount to encroaching on the sovereign's grace—a thing that must not be done."
translations.idiomatic: If this were made public, it would amount to stealing the sovereign's credit—a thing that must never be done."

sentences.zh: 使綜對前焚之。

translations.literal: He had Zong burn it before him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zong burn the edict before him.

sentences.zh: 帝后謂邵曰：「卿之獲免，謝述有力焉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor afterward said to Shao: "Your escape from punishment owed much to Xie Shu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later told Shao, "Your escape from punishment owed much to Xie Shu."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiyou, the Wei ruler went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiyou, the Northern Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙酉，河西王蒙遜遣子安周入待於魏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yiyou, the King of Hexi Meng Xun sent his son Anzhou to attend at the Wei court as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiyou, Meng Xun, King of Hexi, sent his son Anzhou to the Northern Wei court as hostage.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕瑰遣侍郎謝太寧奉表於魏，請送赫連定。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent the Gentleman-Attendant Xie Taining to present a memorial to Wei requesting that Helian Ding be handed over.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent Gentleman-Attendant Xie Taining to present a memorial to Northern Wei requesting that Helian Ding be handed over.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏以慕瑰為大將軍，封西秦王。

translations.literal: On jichou, Wei appointed Murong Gui Grand General and enfeoffed him as King of Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Northern Wei appointed Murong Gui Grand General and enfeoffed him as King of Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 左僕射臨川王義慶固求解職；

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, firmly requested to be relieved of his post;
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, firmly asked to be relieved of his post;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以義慶為中書令，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: on jiachen he was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat, retaining his post as Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: on jiachen he was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat while retaining his post as Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guichou, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, the Northern Wei emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚申，加太尉長孫嵩柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Grand Commandant Zhangsun Song was given the additional title of Pillar of State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Grand Commandant Zhangsun Song was given the additional title Pillar of State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 以左光祿大夫崔浩為司徒，征西大將軍長孫道生為司空。

translations.literal: The Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness Cui Hao was appointed Minister of Education, and the General Who Conquers the West Zhangsun Daosheng was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness, was made Minister of Education, and Zhangsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 道生性清儉，一熊皮鄣泥，數十年不易。

translations.literal: Daosheng was by nature pure and frugal; a single bear-hide mud-guard for his carriage he did not change for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was by nature pure and frugal; he kept a single bear-hide mud-guard on his carriage for decades without replacing it.

sentences.zh: 魏主使歌工歷頌群臣曰：「智如崔浩，廉若道生。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had singing attendants go through the ranks praising the ministers, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, incorrupt as Daosheng."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had singers go through the ranks praising his ministers: "Wise as Cui Hao, incorrupt as Daosheng."

sentences.zh: 魏主欲選使者詣河西，崔浩薦尚書李順，乃以順為太常。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to choose an envoy to go to Hexi; Cui Hao recommended the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Shun, and Shun was appointed Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to choose an envoy to Hexi; Cui Hao recommended Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Shun, who was appointed Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 拜河西王蒙遜為侍中、都督涼州、西域、羌、戎諸軍事、太傅、行征西大將軍、涼州牧、涼王，王武威、張掖、敦煌、酒泉、西海、金城、西平七郡。

translations.literal: The King of Hexi Meng Xun was appointed Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, the Western Regions, Qiang, and Rong, Grand Tutor, Acting General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang, with sovereignty over the seven commanderies of Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Jiuquan, Xihai, Jincheng, and Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun, King of Hexi, was made Palace Attendant, commander of all military affairs in Liangzhou, the Western Regions, Qiang, and Rong, Grand Tutor, Acting General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang, with sovereignty over Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Jiuquan, Xihai, Jincheng, and Xiping.

sentences.zh: 冊曰：「盛衰存亡，與魏升降。

translations.literal: The investiture document read: "In rise and fall, survival and extinction, you shall rise and fall with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture document read, "In rise and fall, survival and extinction, you shall rise and fall with Wei.

sentences.zh: 北盡窮發，南極庸、□昏，西被崑嶺，東至河曲，王實征之，以夾輔皇室。」

translations.literal: North to Qiongfa, south to Yong and [Qiong], west to the Kunlun range, east to the bends of the Yellow River—the King shall truly campaign there to flank and support the imperial house."
translations.idiomatic: North to Qiongfa, south to Yong and Qiong, west to the Kunlun range, east to the bends of the Yellow River—you shall campaign there to flank and support the imperial house."

sentences.zh: 置將相、群卿、百官，承製假授，建天子旌旗，出入警蹕，如漢初諸侯王故事。

translations.literal: He was to set up generals, ministers, the host of officials, and grant provisional appointments by imperial rescript; he might raise the imperial banners and pennons and go in and out with the imperial guard, following the precedent of the feudal kings at the beginning of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He might appoint generals, ministers, and officials, grant provisional appointments by imperial rescript, raise imperial banners and pennons, and go in and out with the imperial guard, following the precedent of the feudal kings at the beginning of Han.

sentences.zh: 壬申，魏主詔曰：「今二寇摧殄，將偃武修文，理廢職，舉逸民。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Wei ruler issued an edict: "Now that the two enemies have been destroyed, we shall cease arms and cultivate culture, restore abolished offices, and raise reclusive worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the Northern Wei emperor issued an edict: "Now that the two enemies have been destroyed, we shall cease arms and cultivate culture, restore abolished offices, and raise reclusive worthies.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧玄、博陵崔綽、趙郡李靈、河間邢穎、勃海高允、廣平游雅、太原張偉等，皆賢俊之冑，冠冕州邦。

translations.literal: Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Cui Chuo of Boling, Li Ling of Zhao, Xing Ying of Hejian, Gao Yun of Bohai, You Ya of Guangping, Zhang Wei of Taiyuan, and others are all scions of worthy talent, the ornaments of their provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Cui Chuo of Boling, Li Ling of Zhao, Xing Ying of Hejian, Gao Yun of Bohai, You Ya of Guangping, Zhang Wei of Taiyuan, and others are all scions of worthy talent, the ornaments of their provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『我有好爵，吾與爾縻之。』

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 'I have fine ranks; I will bind you to them with them.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, 'I have fine ranks; I will bind you to them.'

sentences.zh: 如玄之比者，盡敕州郡以禮發遣。」

translations.literal: Men like Xuan shall all be ordered by the provinces and commanderies to be sent forth with ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xuan shall all be sent forth with ceremony by their provinces and commanderies."

sentences.zh: 遂征玄等及州郡所遣至者數百人，差次敘用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan and the others were summoned, together with several hundred men sent by the provinces and commanderies; they were appointed in graded order.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others were summoned, together with several hundred men sent by the provinces and commanderies, and appointed in graded order.

sentences.zh: 崔綽以母老固辭。

translations.literal: Cui Chuo firmly declined on the grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chuo firmly declined on the grounds that his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 玄等皆拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Xuan and the others were all appointed Erudites of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others were all made Erudites of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄，諶之曾孫；

translations.literal: Xuan was a great-grandson of Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was a great-grandson of Zhen;

sentences.zh: 靈，順之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Ling was a cousin on the father's side of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was a cousin of Shun on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 玄舅崔浩，每與玄言，輒歎曰：「對子真使我懷古之情更深。」

translations.literal: Xuan's uncle Cui Hao, whenever he spoke with Xuan, would sigh and say: "Facing you truly deepens my longing for antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's uncle Cui Hao, whenever he spoke with Xuan, would sigh and say, "Talking with you truly deepens my longing for antiquity."

sentences.zh: 浩欲大整流品，明辨姓族。

translations.literal: Hao wished to overhaul the ranking of clans and clarify surnames and lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wished to overhaul clan rankings and clarify surnames and lineages.

sentences.zh: 玄止之曰：「夫創製立事，各有其時；

translations.literal: Xuan stopped him, saying: "Establishing institutions and founding undertakings each has its proper time;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan stopped him, saying, "Establishing institutions and founding undertakings each has its proper time;

sentences.zh: 樂為此者，詎有幾人！

translations.literal: how many are there who would delight in this!
translations.idiomatic: how many would delight in this!

sentences.zh: 宜加三思。」

translations.literal: You should think thrice about it."
translations.idiomatic: You should think thrice about it."

sentences.zh: 浩不從，由是得罪於眾。

translations.literal: Hao did not listen, and thereby incurred the displeasure of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not listen, and thereby incurred widespread displeasure.

sentences.zh: 初，魏昭成帝始製法令：「反逆者族。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei first made laws and ordinances: "Those guilty of rebellion and treason—the clan is destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Zhaocheng of Northern Wei first enacted laws: "Those guilty of rebellion and treason—the clan is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其餘當死者聽入金、馬贖罪。

translations.literal: For the rest, those who should die may be allowed to redeem guilt with gold and horses.
translations.idiomatic: For other capital offenses, the condemned might redeem guilt with gold and horses.

sentences.zh: 殺人者聽與死家馬牛、葬具以平之。

translations.literal: Murderers might be allowed to give the victim's family horses, cattle, and burial goods to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers might settle matters by giving the victim's family horses, cattle, and burial goods.

sentences.zh: 盜官物，一備五；

translations.literal: Theft of government goods: restitution fivefold;
translations.idiomatic: Theft of government goods: restitution fivefold;

sentences.zh: 私物，一備十。」

translations.literal: private goods, tenfold."
translations.idiomatic: private goods, tenfold."

sentences.zh: 四部大人共坐王庭決辭訟，無系訊連逮之苦，境內安之。

translations.literal: The four tribal chieftains together sat in the royal court to decide lawsuits; there was no suffering of imprisonment, interrogation, or chain arrest, and the realm within was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The four tribal chieftains together sat in the royal court to decide lawsuits; there was no imprisonment, interrogation, or chain arrest, and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 太祖入中原，患前代律令峻密，命三公郎王德刪定，務崇簡易。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, on entering the Central Plains, was troubled that the laws and ordinances of former dynasties were harsh and dense; he ordered the Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Wang De to revise and fix them, striving for simplicity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, on entering the Central Plains, found the laws of former dynasties harsh and dense; he ordered Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Wang De to revise them, striving for simplicity.

sentences.zh: 季年被疾，刑罰濫酷；

translations.literal: In his later years he fell ill, and punishments became excessive and cruel;
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he fell ill, and punishments grew excessive and cruel;

sentences.zh: 太宗承之，吏文亦深。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong inherited this, and official documents also grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong inherited this, and official documents grew severe as well.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，世祖命崔浩更定律令，除五歲、四歲刑，增一年刑；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Emperor Shizu ordered Cui Hao to revise the laws and ordinances, abolishing the punishments of five and four years and adding the punishment of one year;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Emperor Shizu ordered Cui Hao to revise the laws, abolishing the punishments of five and four years and adding the punishment of one year;

sentences.zh: 巫蠱者，負羖羊、抱犬沉諸淵。

translations.literal: those guilty of witchcraft and sorcery were to bear a ram on their backs, hold a dog in their arms, and be drowned in a deep pool.
translations.idiomatic: those guilty of witchcraft were to bear a ram on their backs, hold a dog in their arms, and be drowned in a deep pool.

sentences.zh: 初令官階九品者得以官爵除刑。

translations.literal: For the first time it was ordained that those of the nine official ranks might commute punishment by office and title.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time it was ordained that officials of the nine ranks might commute punishment by office and title.

sentences.zh: 婦人當刑而孕，產後百日乃決。

translations.literal: Women who should be punished but were pregnant were not sentenced until a hundred days after giving birth.
translations.idiomatic: Women due for punishment but pregnant were not sentenced until a hundred days after giving birth.

sentences.zh: 闕左懸登聞鼓，以達冤人。

translations.literal: To the left of the palace gate was hung the "Appeal-to-the-Throne" drum, so that the wronged might be heard.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of the palace gate hung the Appeal-to-the-Throne drum, so that the wronged might be heard.

sentences.zh: 魏主如漠南，十一月，丙辰，北部敕勒莫弗庫若干帥所部數萬騎，驅鹿數百萬頭，詣魏主行在。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler went to the southern desert. In the eleventh month, on bingchen, the northern Tiele chieftain Kugan led several tens of thousands of horsemen of his tribe, driving several million head of deer, to the Wei ruler's traveling encampment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the southern desert. In the eleventh month, on bingchen, the northern Tiele chieftain Kugan led tens of thousands of horsemen, driving millions of deer, to the emperor's traveling encampment.

sentences.zh: 魏主大獵以賜從官。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler held a great hunt and bestowed the game on the attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a great hunt and bestowed the game on the attending officials.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁丑，還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，涼王改元義和。

translations.literal: That year, the King of Liang changed the era name to Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the King of Liang changed the era name to Yihe.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范陽邁寇九德，交州兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: The King of Linyi, Fan Yangmai, raided Jiude; the troops of Jiaozhou struck and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yangmai, King of Linyi, raided Jiude; the troops of Jiaozhou struck and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之下元嘉九年（

translations.literal: The lower part of "Emperor Wen of the Ancestor [dynasty], Part One" — Yuanjia year 9 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, Part One (continued) — Yuanjia year 9 (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元四三二年）

translations.literal: renshen, corresponding to 432 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renshen, corresponding to 432 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午，魏主尊保太后竇氏為皇太后，立貴人赫連氏為皇后，子晃為皇太子。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingwu, the Wei ruler honored the Dowager Empress of Assurance, Lady Dou, as Empress Dowager, installed the Honored Lady Helian as empress, and made his son Huang crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingwu, the Northern Wei emperor honored Dowager Empress of Assurance Lady Dou as Empress Dowager, installed Honored Lady Helian as empress, and made his son Huang crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元延和。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 燕王立慕容後之子王仁為太子。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler installed Murong Hou's son Wang Ren as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Northern Yan installed Murong Hou's son Wang Ren as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，衛將軍王弘進位太保，加中書監。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengxu, the General of the Guard Wang Hong was promoted to Grand Tutor with added appointment as Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengxu, General of the Guard Wang Hong was promoted to Grand Tutor with added appointment as Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，征南大將軍檀道濟進位司空，還鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji was promoted to Minister of Works and returned to garrison Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji was promoted to Minister of Works and returned to garrison Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，吐谷渾王慕瑰送赫連定於魏，魏人殺之。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent Helian Ding to Wei, and the Wei people killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent Helian Ding to Northern Wei, and the Northern Wei killed him.

sentences.zh: 慕瑰上表曰：「臣俘擒僭逆，獻捷王府，爵秩雖崇而士不增廓，車旗既飾而財不周賞，願垂鑒察。」

translations.literal: Murong Gui submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant captured the usurper and rebel and presented the victory to the royal house. Though rank and title are lofty, my territory has not been enlarged; though chariots and banners are adorned, my wealth is insufficient for rewards. I beg Your Majesty to take note."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant captured the usurper and presented the victory to the royal house. Though rank and title are lofty, my territory has not been enlarged; though chariots and banners are adorned, my wealth is insufficient for rewards. I beg Your Majesty to take note."

sentences.zh: 魏主下其議。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler referred it for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred it for discussion.

sentences.zh: 公卿以為：「慕瑰所致唯定而已，塞外之民皆為己有，而貪求無厭，不可許也。」

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers held: "What Murong Gui presented was only Ding; the peoples beyond the passes are all already his, yet he is insatiably greedy—this cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The dukes and ministers held, "What Murong Gui presented was only Ding; the peoples beyond the passes are already his, yet he is insatiably greedy—this cannot be granted."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃詔曰：「西秦王所得金城、枹罕、隴西之地，朕即與之，乃是裂土，何須復廓。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler then issued an edict: "The lands of Jincheng, Fuhan, and Longxi that the King of Western Qin received—I gave them to him at once; that was already a division of territory—why must it be enlarged again?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict: "The lands of Jincheng, Fuhan, and Longxi that the King of Western Qin received—I gave them to him at once; that was already a division of territory—why must it be enlarged again?

sentences.zh: 西秦款至，綿絹隨使疏數，臨時增益，非一賜而止也。」

translations.literal: When Western Qin shows sincere allegiance, silk and floss follow the envoys in frequent shipments, with added grants as occasion arises—not a single bestowal and no more."
translations.idiomatic: When Western Qin shows sincere allegiance, silk and floss follow the envoys in frequent shipments, with added grants as occasion arises—not a single bestowal and no more."

sentences.zh: 自是慕瑰貢使至魏者稍簡。

translations.literal: From this time Murong Gui's tribute envoys to Wei became somewhat fewer.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Murong Gui's tribute envoys to Northern Wei became somewhat fewer.

sentences.zh: 魏方士祁纖奏改代為萬年，以代尹為萬年尹，代令為萬年令。

translations.literal: The Wei adept Qi Xian memorialized to change Dai to Wannian, the Intendant of Dai to Intendant of Wannian, and the Magistrate of Dai to Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei adept Qi Xian memorialized to change Dai to Wannian, the Intendant of Dai to Intendant of Wannian, and the Magistrate of Dai to Magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 崔浩曰：「昔太祖應天受命，兼稱代、魏以法殷商。

translations.literal: Cui Hao said: "Formerly the Founding Emperor responded to Heaven and received the Mandate, using both Dai and Wei in the manner of the Yin-Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao said, "Formerly the Founding Emperor responded to Heaven and received the Mandate, using both Dai and Wei in the manner of the Yin-Shang.

sentences.zh: 國家積德，當享年萬億，不待假名以為益也。

translations.literal: The state has accumulated virtue and should enjoy ten thousand myriad years—there is no need to borrow a name for added benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The state has accumulated virtue and should enjoy ten thousand myriad years—there is no need to borrow a name for added benefit.

sentences.zh: 纖之所聞，皆非正義，復舊號。」

translations.literal: What Xian has heard is all contrary to right principle; restore the old designations."
translations.idiomatic: What Xian proposes is all contrary to right principle; restore the old designations."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬申，華容文昭公王弘卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on renshen, the Duke of Literary Brilliance of Huarong, Wang Hong, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on renshen, Wang Hong, Duke of Literary Brilliance of Huarong, died.

sentences.zh: 弘明敏有思致，而輕率少威儀，性褊隘，好折辱人，人以此少之。

translations.literal: Hong was bright and keen with thoughtful insight, but was frivolous and lacked dignity; by nature narrow-minded, he liked to humiliate others, and for this people thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was bright and keen with thoughtful insight, but frivolous and lacking dignity; narrow-minded by nature, he liked to humiliate others, and for this people thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 雖貴顯，不營財利；

translations.literal: Though noble and eminent, he did not pursue wealth and profit;
translations.idiomatic: Though noble and eminent, he did not pursue wealth;

sentences.zh: 及卒，家無餘業。

translations.literal: when he died, the family had no surplus estate.
translations.idiomatic: when he died, his family had no surplus estate.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，特賜錢百萬，米千斛。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he specially bestowed a million cash and a thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he specially bestowed a million cash and a thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 魏主治兵於南郊，謀伐燕。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler drilled troops at the southern suburb, planning to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor drilled troops at the southern suburb, planning to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者趙道生聘於魏。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the envoy Zhao Daosheng on a friendly mission to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor sent envoy Zhao Daosheng on a friendly mission to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊寅，司徒、南徐州刺史彭城王義康改領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuyin, the Minister of Education and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, was changed to Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuyin, Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, Minister of Education and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was reassigned as Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔分青州置冀州，治歷城。

translations.literal: An edict divided Qingzhou to establish Jizhou, with its seat at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict divided Qingzhou to establish Jizhou, with its seat at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕瑰遣其司馬趙叔入貢，且來告捷。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent his Chief Administrator Zhao Shu to present tribute and also to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king Murong Gui sent his Chief Administrator Zhao Shu to present tribute and report victory.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主伐燕。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Wei ruler attacked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the Northern Wei emperor attacked Yan.

sentences.zh: 命太子晃錄尚書事，時晃才五歲。

translations.literal: He ordered the crown prince Huang to record affairs of the Imperial Secretariat; Huang was then only five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Crown Prince Huang to record affairs of the Imperial Secretariat; Huang was then only five years old.

sentences.zh: 又遣左僕射安原、建寧王崇等屯漠南以備柔然。

translations.literal: He also sent the Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Anyuan, the Prince of Jianning Chong, and others to encamp in the southern desert to guard against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Left Vice Director Anyuan, Prince of Jianning Chong, and others to encamp in the southern desert to guard against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏主遣散騎常侍鄧穎來聘。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Wei ruler sent the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Deng Ying on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the Northern Wei emperor sent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Deng Ying on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以吐谷渾王慕瑰為都督西秦、河、沙三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、西秦、河二州刺史，進爵隴西王，且命慕瑰悉歸南方將士先沒於夏者，得百五十餘人。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Tuyuhun king Murong Gui was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Conquers the West, Inspector of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, with advancement in rank to King of Longxi; he was also ordered to return all southern officers and soldiers previously lost to Xia, numbering more than a hundred and fifty.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Murong Gui was appointed commander of all military affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Conquers the West, and Inspector of Western Qin and He, with advancement to King of Longxi; he was also ordered to return all southern officers and soldiers previously lost to Xia, numbering more than a hundred and fifty.

sentences.zh: 又加北秦州刺史楊難當征西將軍。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, was also given the additional title of General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, was also given the additional title General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 難當以兄子保宗為鎮將軍，鎮宕昌；

translations.literal: Nandang appointed his elder brother's son Baozong Garrison General, to garrison Dangchang;
translations.idiomatic: Nandang appointed his nephew Baozong Garrison General to garrison Dangchang;

sentences.zh: 以其子為秦州刺史，守上邽。

translations.literal: and his son Inspector of Qinzhou, to hold Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: and his son Inspector of Qinzhou to hold Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 保宗謀襲難當，事洩，難當囚之。

translations.literal: Baozong plotted to attack Nandang; when the affair leaked out, Nandang imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Baozong plotted to attack Nandang; when the plot leaked out, Nandang imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以江夏王義恭為都督南袞等六州諸軍事、開府儀同三司、南袞州刺史，臨川王義慶為都督荊、雍等七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，竟陵王義宣為中書監，衡陽王義秀為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the six provinces including Southern Yan and others, with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Southern Yan; the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the seven provinces including Jing and Yong and others, and Inspector of Jingzhou; the Prince of Jingling Yixuan was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat; and the Prince of Hengyang Yixiu was appointed Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, was made commander of six provinces including Southern Yan, with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Southern Yan; Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan, was made commander of seven provinces including Jing and Yong and Inspector of Jingzhou; Yixuan, Prince of Jingling, was made Supervisor of the Secretariat; and Yixiu, Prince of Hengyang, was made Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以刑州居上流之重，土地廣遠，資實兵甲居朝廷之半，故遺詔令諸子居之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gaozu, because Jingzhou occupied the weighty position of the upper reaches, with broad and distant territory and resources and armor amounting to half the court's, left instructions in his testamentary edict that his sons should reside there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Jingzhou occupied the strategic upper reaches, with broad territory and resources and armor amounting to half the court's stores, Emperor Gaozu left instructions in his testamentary edict that his sons should reside there.

sentences.zh: 上以義慶宗室令美，且烈武王有大功於社稷，故特用之。

translations.literal: The present Emperor, because Yiqing was of the imperial house and outstanding in excellence, and because Prince Lieuwu had great merit toward the altars of soil and grain, especially appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor, because Yiqing was of the imperial house and outstanding in excellence, and because Prince Lieuwu had great merit toward the state, especially appointed him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己未，魏主至濡水。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiwei, the Wei ruler reached the Ru River.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiwei, the Northern Wei emperor reached the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 庚申，遣安東將軍奚斤發幽州民及密雲丁零萬餘人，運攻具，出南道，會和龍。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he sent the General Who Pacifies the East Xi Jin to mobilize the people of Youzhou and more than ten thousand Dingling of Miyun, transport siege equipment, advance by the southern route, and join at Helong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, he sent General Who Pacifies the East Xi Jin to mobilize the people of Youzhou and more than ten thousand Dingling of Miyun, transport siege equipment, advance by the southern route, and join at Helong.

sentences.zh: 魏主至遼西，燕王遣其侍御史崔聘奉牛酒犒師。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler reached Liaoxi, the Yan king sent his Attendant Censor Cui Pin to present cattle and wine to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Liaoxi, the Yan king sent Attendant Censor Cui Pin to present cattle and wine to comfort the army.

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏主至和龍。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Wei ruler reached Helong.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the Northern Wei emperor reached Helong.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以領軍將軍殷景仁為尚書僕射，太子詹事劉湛為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Liu Zhan was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Liu Zhan was made General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉道濟，粹之弟也，信任長史費謙、別駕張熙等，聚斂興利，傷政害民，立官冶，禁民鼓鑄而貴賣鐵器，商賈失業，吁嗟滿路。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yizhou Liu Daoji was a younger brother of Cui. He trusted the Chief Administrator Fei Qian, the Vice Director Zhang Xi, and others, who amassed wealth and pursued profit, harming government and injuring the people; they established official smelters, forbade the people to cast iron while selling ironware at high prices; merchants lost their livelihoods, and lamentation filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoji, Inspector of Yizhou, was a younger brother of Cui. He trusted Chief Administrator Fei Qian, Vice Director Zhang Xi, and others, who amassed wealth and pursued profit, harming government and injuring the people; they established official smelters, forbade the people to cast iron while selling ironware at high prices; merchants lost their livelihoods, and lamentation filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 流民許穆之，變姓名稱司馬飛龍，自雲晉室近親，往依氐王楊難當。

translations.literal: The displaced person Xu Muzhi changed his name and styled himself Sima Feilong, claiming to be a close kinsman of the Jin house; he went to rely on the Di king Yang Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced person Xu Muzhi changed his name and styled himself Sima Feilong, claiming to be a close kinsman of the Jin house; he went to rely on the Di king Yang Nandang.

sentences.zh: 難當因民之怨，資飛龍以兵，使侵擾益州。

translations.literal: Nandang, taking advantage of the people's resentment, supplied Feilong with troops and had him harass Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang, taking advantage of popular resentment, supplied Feilong with troops and had him harass Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 飛龍招合蜀人，得千餘人，攻殺巴興令，逐陰平太守；

translations.literal: Feilong gathered Shu people, obtaining more than a thousand men; he attacked and killed the magistrate of Baxing and drove out the Administrator of Yinping;
translations.idiomatic: Feilong gathered Shu followers, obtaining more than a thousand men; he attacked and killed the magistrate of Baxing and drove out the Administrator of Yinping;

sentences.zh: 道濟遣軍擊斬之。

translations.literal: Daoji sent troops who struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji sent troops who struck and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 道濟欲以五城人制氐奴、梁顯為參軍督護，費謙固執不與。

translations.literal: Daoji wished to appoint the men of Wucheng, Zhinu and Liang Xian, as military adjutants and supervisors; Fei Qian stubbornly refused to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji wished to appoint Zhinu and Liang Xian of Wucheng as military adjutants and supervisors; Fei Qian stubbornly refused.

sentences.zh: 氐奴等與鄉人趙廣構扇縣人，詐言司馬殿下猶在陽泉山中，聚眾得數千人，引向廣漢；

translations.literal: Zhinu and the others, with their fellow townsman Zhao Guang, incited the county people, falsely claiming that the Sima prince was still in Yangquan mountain; they gathered several thousand men and marched toward Guanghan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhinu and the others, with their fellow townsman Zhao Guang, incited the county people, falsely claiming that the Sima prince was still on Yangquan mountain; they gathered several thousand men and marched toward Guanghan;

sentences.zh: 道濟參軍程展會治中李抗之，將五百人擊之，皆敗死。

translations.literal: Daoji's military adjutant Cheng Zhanhui and the Administrator of the Palace Li Kangzhi led five hundred men to attack them and were all defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's adjutant Cheng Zhanhui and Palace Administrator Li Kangzhi led five hundred men to attack them and were all defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 巴西人詔唐頻聚眾應之，趙廣等進攻涪城，陷之。

translations.literal: Zhao Tangpin of Baxi gathered a crowd in response; Zhao Guang and the others advanced to attack Fucheng and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tangpin of Baxi gathered followers in response; Zhao Guang and the others advanced on Fucheng and captured it.

sentences.zh: 於是涪陵、江陽、遂寧諸郡守皆棄城走，蜀土僑、舊俱反。

translations.literal: Thereupon the administrators of Fuling, Jiangyang, Suining, and other commanderies all abandoned their cities and fled; migrants and native residents throughout Shu all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the administrators of Fuling, Jiangyang, Suining, and other commanderies all abandoned their cities and fled, and migrants and native residents throughout Shu rose in revolt together.

sentences.zh: 燕石城太守李崇等十郡降於魏。

translations.literal: Li Chong, Administrator of Yanshi, and ten commanderies surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Administrator of Yanshi, and the governors of ten commanderies surrendered to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主發其民三萬穿圍暫以守和龍。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler mobilized thirty thousand of their people to dig entrenchments as a temporary defense of Helong.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor mobilized thirty thousand of their people to dig entrenchments as a temporary defense of Helong.

sentences.zh: 崇，績之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was the son of Li Ji.

sentences.zh: 八月，燕王使數萬人出戰，魏昌黎公丘等擊破之，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Yan king sent tens of thousands of men out to give battle; the Wei Duke of Changli, Qiu, and others struck and routed them, and more than ten thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Yan king sent tens of thousands of men out to fight; the Northern Wei Duke of Changli, Qiu, and others routed them, and more than ten thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 燕尚書高紹帥萬餘家保羌胡固；

translations.literal: The Yan Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Gao Shao led more than ten thousand households to hold Qianghu Fort;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yan Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Gao Shao led more than ten thousand households to hold Qianghu Fort;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏主攻紹，斬之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Wei ruler attacked Shao and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Northern Wei emperor attacked Gao Shao and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 平東將軍賀多羅攻帶方，撫軍大將軍永昌王健攻建德，驃騎大將軍樂平王丕攻冀陽，皆拔之。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the East He Duoluo attacked Daifang; the General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the Army Yongchang Wang Jian attacked Jiande; the General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry the Prince of Leping Pi attacked Jiyang; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the East He Duoluo took Daifang; General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the Army Wang Jian of Yongchang took Jiande; and General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry the Prince of Leping, Pi, took Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，魏主引兵西還，徙營丘、成周、遼東、樂浪、帶方、玄菟六郡民三萬家於幽州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, the Wei ruler led his army back west and moved thirty thousand households from the six commanderies of Yingqiu, Chengdong, Liaodong, Lelang, Daifang, and Xuantu to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, the Northern Wei emperor led his army back west and relocated thirty thousand households from the six commanderies of Yingqiu, Chengdong, Liaodong, Lelang, Daifang, and Xuantu to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕尚書郭淵勸燕王送款獻女於魏，乞為附庸。

translations.literal: The Yan Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Guo Yuan urged the Yan king to send tokens of submission and offer a daughter to Wei, begging to become a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yan Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Guo Yuan urged the Yan king to submit and offer a daughter to the Northern Wei, begging to become a vassal state.

sentences.zh: 燕王曰：「負釁在前，結忿已深，降附取死，不如守志更圖也。」

translations.literal: The Yan king said: "Guilt lies upon us already, and enmity has been deeply fixed; to surrender and submit is to court death. Better to hold to our resolve and seek another plan."
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king said, "We already bear guilt on our record, and enmity has sunk deep; to surrender would be to court death. Better to hold firm and look for another way."

sentences.zh: 魏主之圍和龍也，宿衛之士多在戰陳，行宮人少。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler was besieging Helong, most of the palace guard were in the battle lines, and the mobile palace had few men.
translations.idiomatic: While the Northern Wei emperor was besieging Helong, most of the palace guard were in the battle lines, and the mobile palace was lightly manned.

sentences.zh: 雲中鎮將朱受之謀與南人襲殺魏主，因入和龍，浮海南歸；

translations.literal: Zhu Shouzhi, garrison commander of Yunzhong, plotted with southerners to surprise and kill the Wei ruler, then enter Helong and return south by sea;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouzhi, garrison commander of Yunzhong, plotted with southerners to surprise and kill the Northern Wei emperor, then enter Helong and return south by sea;

sentences.zh: 以告冠軍將軍毛修之，毛修之不從，乃止。

translations.literal: he told the General Who Conquers the Enemy Mao Xiuzhi, but Mao Xiuzhi would not follow, and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He told General Who Conquers the Enemy Mao Xiuzhi, but Mao Xiuzhi refused to go along, and the plot was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 既而事洩，朱修之逃奔燕。

translations.literal: Before long the matter leaked out, and Zhu Xiuzhi fled to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the plot leaked out, and Zhu Xiuzhi fled to Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 魏人數伐燕，燕王遣修之南歸求救。

translations.literal: Wei repeatedly attacked Yan, and the Yan king sent Xiuzhi south to return and seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As the Northern Wei repeatedly attacked Yan, the Yan king sent Xiuzhi south to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 修之泛海至東萊，遂還建康，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi crossed the sea to Donglai, then returned to Jiankang and was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi crossed the sea to Donglai, returned to Jiankang, and was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 趙廣等進攻成都，劉道濟嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang and the others advanced to attack Chengdu; Liu Daoji tightened the city defenses and held out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang and the others advanced on Chengdu, and Liu Daoji tightened the defenses and held the city.

sentences.zh: 賊眾頓聚日久，不見司馬飛龍，欲散去。

translations.literal: The rebel host had camped together for a long time without seeing Sima Feilong and wished to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had camped together for a long time without seeing Sima Feilong and were ready to disperse.

sentences.zh: 廣懼，將三千人及羽儀詣陽泉寺，詐雲迎飛龍。

translations.literal: Guang, in fear, led three thousand men and ceremonial guards to Yangquan Temple, falsely claiming he was going to welcome Feilong.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, alarmed, led three thousand men and ceremonial guards to Yangquan Temple, falsely claiming he was going to welcome Feilong.

sentences.zh: 至則謂道人枹罕程道養曰：「汝但自言是飛龍，則坐享富貴；

translations.literal: When he arrived he said to the Daoist monk Cheng Daoyang of Baohen: "You need only declare yourself Feilong, and you will sit and enjoy wealth and rank;
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he said to the Daoist monk Cheng Daoyang of Baohen, "You need only declare yourself Feilong, and you will sit back and enjoy wealth and rank;

sentences.zh: 不則斷頭！」

translations.literal: otherwise I will cut off your head!"
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I will cut off your head!"

sentences.zh: 道養惶怖許諾。

translations.literal: Daoyang, terrified, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyang, terrified, agreed.

sentences.zh: 廣乃推道養為蜀王、車騎大將軍、益、梁二州牧，改元泰始，備置百官。

translations.literal: Guang then set up Daoyang as King of Shu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of the two provinces of Yi and Liang; he changed the era name to Taishi and fully established the ranks of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guang then set up Daoyang as King of Shu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Yi and Liang; he changed the era name to Taishi and established a full roster of officials.

sentences.zh: 以道養弟道助為驃騎將軍、長沙王，鎮涪城；

translations.literal: He made Daoyang's younger brother Daozhu General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Changsha, stationed at Fucheng;
translations.idiomatic: He made Daoyang's younger brother Daozhu General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Changsha, with his base at Fucheng;

sentences.zh: 趙廣、帛氐奴、梁顯及其黨張尋、嚴遐皆為將軍，奉道養還成都，眾至十餘萬，四面圍城，使人謂道濟曰：「但送費謙、張熙來，我輩自解去。」

translations.literal: Zhao Guang, Bo Dinu, Liang Xian, and their followers Zhang Xun and Yan Xia were all made generals; they escorted Daoyang back to Chengdu. The host reached more than one hundred thousand, besieging the city on all sides, and sent someone to tell Daoji: "Just send Fei Qian and Zhang Xi to us, and we will disband and leave of ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang, Bo Dinu, Liang Xian, and their followers Zhang Xun and Yan Xia were all made generals and escorted Daoyang back to Chengdu. Their force grew to more than one hundred thousand and besieged the city on all sides; they sent word to Daoji, "Just hand over Fei Qian and Zhang Xi, and we will disband and leave on our own."

sentences.zh: 道濟遣中兵參軍裴方明、任浪之各將千餘人出戰，皆敗還。

translations.literal: Daoji sent the Central Army Adjutants Pei Fangming and Ren Langzhi, each leading more than a thousand men, out to give battle; all were defeated and driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji sent Central Army Adjutants Pei Fangming and Ren Langzhi, each leading more than a thousand men, out to fight; both were defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，乙巳，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on yisi, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on yisi, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以少府中山甄法崇為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On renzi, Zhen Fachong of Zhongshan, Director of the Palace Provisionery, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Zhen Fachong of Zhongshan, Director of the Palace Provisionery, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，燕王嫡妃王氏，生長樂公崇，崇于兄弟為最長。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Yan king's principal consort, Lady Wang, bore the Duke of Changle, Chong; among the brothers Chong was the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Yan king's principal consort, Lady Wang, had borne the Duke of Changle, Chong, who was the eldest among the brothers.

sentences.zh: 及即位，立慕容氏為王后，王氏不得立，又黜崇，使鎮肥如。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he installed Lady Murong as queen; Lady Wang was not installed, and Chong was also demoted and sent to garrison Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he installed Lady Murong as queen; Lady Wang was passed over, and Chong was demoted and sent to garrison Feiru.

sentences.zh: 崇母弟廣平公朗、樂陵公邈相謂曰：「今國家將亡，人無愚智皆知之。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brothers by the same mother, the Duke of Guangping Lang and the Duke of Leling Miao, said to each other: "The state is about to perish; everyone, wise or foolish, knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brothers by the same mother, Lang, Duke of Guangping, and Miao, Duke of Leling, said to each other, "The state is about to fall, and everyone, wise or foolish, knows it.

sentences.zh: 王復受慕容後譖，吾兄弟死無日矣！」

translations.literal: The king again accepts the slanders of Empress Murong; our brothers' days are numbered!"
translations.idiomatic: The king again listens to Empress Murong's slanders; our days are numbered!"

sentences.zh: 乃相與亡奔遼西，說崇使降魏，崇從之。

translations.literal: They then fled together to Liaoxi and urged Chong to surrender to Wei; Chong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: They then fled together to Liaoxi and urged Chong to surrender to the Northern Wei; Chong agreed.

sentences.zh: 會魏主使給事郎王德招崇，十二月，己丑，崇使邈如魏，請舉郡降。

translations.literal: Just then the Wei ruler sent the Attendant Wang De to win Chong over; in the twelfth month, on jichou, Chong sent Miao to Wei to request surrender of the whole commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Northern Wei emperor sent Attendant Wang De to win Chong over; in the twelfth month, on jichou, Chong sent Miao to Wei to offer the surrender of the whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 燕王聞之，使其將封羽圍崇於遼西。

translations.literal: When the Yan king heard of it, he sent his general Feng Yu to besiege Chong in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan king heard of it, he sent his general Feng Yu to besiege Chong in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 魏主征諸名士之未仕者，州郡多逼遣之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler summoned eminent scholars who had not yet entered office, and the provinces and commanderies largely forced them to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor summoned eminent scholars who had not yet entered office, and the provinces and commanderies largely forced them to go.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，下詔令守宰以禮申諭，任其進退，毋得逼遣。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler heard of it, he issued an edict ordering the prefects and administrators to explain matters by ritual and persuade them, leaving advance or withdrawal to their choice and forbidding forced dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei emperor heard of it, he issued an edict ordering local officials to explain matters courteously and persuade them, leaving the choice to them and forbidding forced dispatch.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以少子紹為廬陵孝獻王嗣，以江夏王義恭子郎為營陽王嗣；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor made his youngest son Shao heir to Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, and Lang, son of the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, heir to the Prince of Yingyang;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had made his youngest son Shao heir to Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, and Lang, son of Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, heir to the Prince of Yingyang;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，封紹為廬陵王，郎為南豐縣王。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Shao was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling, and Lang as Prince of Nanfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Shao was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling, and Lang as Prince of Nanfeng County.

sentences.zh: 裴方明等復出擊程道養營，破之，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: Pei Fangming and the others again went out and attacked Cheng Daoyang's camp, defeated them, and burned their stores.
