translations.idiomatic: Pei Fangming and the others again went out, attacked Cheng Daoyang's camp, routed them, and burned their stores.

sentences.zh: 賊黨江陽楊孟子將千餘人屯城南，參軍梁俊之統南樓，投書說諭孟子，邀使入城見劉道濟，道濟版為主簿，剋期討賊。

translations.literal: The rebel partisan Yang Mengzi of Jiangyang led more than a thousand men encamped south of the city; the adjutant Liang Junzhi commanded the South Tower, sent a letter to persuade Mengzi, and invited him into the city to see Liu Daoji; Daoji appointed him Chief Secretary by written order and set a date to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Yang Mengzi of Jiangyang led more than a thousand men encamped south of the city; Adjutant Liang Junzhi, commanding the South Tower, sent a letter to win him over and invited him into the city to see Liu Daoji; Daoji appointed him Chief Secretary by written order and set a date to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 趙廣知其謀，孟子懼，將所領奔晉原，晉原太守文仲興與之同拒守。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang learned of the plot; Mengzi, in fear, led those under his command to flee to Jinyuan; the Administrator of Jinyuan Wen Zhongxing joined him in holding out together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang learned of the plot; Mengzi, alarmed, led his men to Jinyuan, where Administrator Wen Zhongxing joined him in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 趙廣遣帛氐奴攻晉原，破之，仲興、孟子皆死。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang sent Bo Dinu to attack Jinyuan, defeated it, and both Zhongxing and Mengzi were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang sent Bo Dinu to attack Jinyuan, took the city, and both Zhongxing and Mengzi were killed.

sentences.zh: 裴方明復出擊賊，屢戰，破之，賊遂大潰；

translations.literal: Pei Fangming again went out and attacked the rebels; after repeated battles he defeated them, and the rebels then broke in great rout;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Fangming again went out against the rebels; after repeated battles he broke them, and they collapsed in rout;

sentences.zh: 程道養收眾得七千人，還廣漢，趙廣別將五千餘人還涪城。

translations.literal: Cheng Daoyang gathered his forces and obtained seven thousand men, returning to Guanghan; Zhao Guang's detached commander led more than five thousand men back to Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Daoyang rallied seven thousand men and withdrew to Guanghan; Zhao Guang's detached commander led more than five thousand men back to Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，張熙說道濟糶倉谷，故自九月末圍城至十二月，糧儲俱盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Xi had urged Daoji to sell off the granary grain, so from the end of the ninth month, when the siege began, until the twelfth month, grain stores were entirely exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Xi had urged Daoji to sell off the granary grain, so from the end of the ninth month, when the siege began, until the twelfth month, the city's grain stores were entirely exhausted.

sentences.zh: 方明將二千人出城求食，為賊所敗，單馬獨還，賊眾復大集。

translations.literal: Fangming led two thousand men out of the city to seek food, was defeated by the rebels, and returned alone on a single horse; the rebel host again gathered in force.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming led two thousand men out of the city to forage for food, was defeated by the rebels, and returned alone on a single horse; the rebels again gathered in force.

sentences.zh: 方明夜縋而上，道濟為設食，涕泣不能食。

translations.literal: Fangming was hauled up by rope in the night; Daoji set out food for him, but he wept and could not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming was hauled up by rope in the night; Daoji set out food for him, but he wept and could not eat.

sentences.zh: 道濟曰：「卿非大丈夫，小敗何苦！

translations.literal: Daoji said: "You are no true man—why grieve over a small defeat!
translations.idiomatic: Daoji said, "You are no true man of spirit—why grieve over a small defeat!

sentences.zh: 賊勢既衰，台兵垂至，但令卿還，何憂於賊！」

translations.literal: The rebels' strength is already waning, and the capital troops are nearly here; I need only send you back—what worry is there about the rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are already weakening, and imperial troops are nearly here; I need only send you back out—what is there to fear from the rebels!"

sentences.zh: 即減左右以配之。

translations.literal: He then reduced his own attendants and reassigned them to Fangming.
translations.idiomatic: He then reduced his own attendants and reassigned them to Fangming.

sentences.zh: 賊於城外揚言，云「方明已死」，城中大恐。

translations.literal: Outside the city the rebels spread word, saying "Fangming is already dead," and great fear arose within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the city the rebels spread word, saying "Fangming is already dead," and panic swept the city.

sentences.zh: 道濟夜列炬火，出方明以示眾，眾乃安。

translations.literal: Daoji lined torches by night, brought Fangming out to show the people, and the people then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji lined torches by night, brought Fangming out to show the people, and the city settled.

sentences.zh: 道濟悉出財物於北射堂，令方明募人。

translations.literal: Daoji brought out all his valuables at the North Archery Hall and had Fangming recruit men.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji brought out all his valuables at the North Archery Hall and had Fangming recruit men.

sentences.zh: 時城中或傳道濟已死，莫有應者。

translations.literal: At the time some in the city spread word that Daoji was already dead, and no one responded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some in the city spread word that Daoji was dead, and no one responded.

sentences.zh: 梁俊之說道濟遣左右給使三十餘人出外，且告之曰：「吾病小損，各聽歸家休息。」

translations.literal: Liang Junzhi advised Daoji to send more than thirty personal attendants and servants outside, and also tell them: "My illness has eased a little; each of you may return home to rest."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Junzhi advised Daoji to send more than thirty personal attendants and servants outside, telling them, "My illness has eased a little; each of you may go home and rest."

sentences.zh: 給使既出，城中乃安，應募者日有千餘人。

translations.literal: Once the attendants had gone out, the city then settled, and more than a thousand men enlisted each day.
translations.idiomatic: Once the attendants had gone out, the city settled, and more than a thousand men enlisted each day.

sentences.zh: 初，晉謝混尚晉陵公主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xie Hun of Jin married Princess Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xie Hun of Jin had married Princess Jinling.

sentences.zh: 混死，詔公主與謝氏絕婚；

translations.literal: When Hun died, an edict ordered the princess to sever marriage with the Xie clan;
translations.idiomatic: When Hun died, an edict ordered the princess to sever ties with the Xie clan;

sentences.zh: 公主悉以混家事委混從子弘微。

translations.literal: the princess entrusted all of Hun's household affairs to Hun's clansman Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: the princess entrusted all of Hun's household affairs to his clansman Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 混仍世宰輔，僮僕千人，唯有二女，年數歲，弘微為之紀理生業，一錢尺帛有文簿。

translations.literal: Hun's family had been chief ministers for generations, with a thousand servants; there were only two daughters, a few years old. Hongwei managed their livelihood for them, and every coin and foot of cloth had its written record.
translations.idiomatic: The Xie family had been chief ministers for generations, with a thousand servants; Hun left only two daughters, still only a few years old. Hongwei managed their estate for them, and every coin and foot of cloth had its written record.

sentences.zh: 九年而高祖即位，公主降號東鄉君，聽還謝氏。

translations.literal: Nine years later Gaozu took the throne; the princess was reduced in rank to Lady of Dongxiang and permitted to return to the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later Emperor Gaozu took the throne; the princess was reduced in rank to Lady of Dongxiang and permitted to return to the Xie household.

sentences.zh: 入門，室宇倉廩，不異平日，田疇墾闢，有加於舊。

translations.literal: When she entered the gate, the buildings and granaries were no different from ordinary days, and the fields under cultivation exceeded what they had been before.
translations.idiomatic: When she entered the gate, the buildings and granaries were unchanged from ordinary days, and the fields under cultivation exceeded what they had been before.

sentences.zh: 東鄉君歎曰：「僕射平生重此子，可謂知人；

translations.literal: Lady Dongxiang sighed and said: "The Vice Director valued this boy all his life—one may truly call that knowing men;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dongxiang sighed and said, "The Vice Director valued this boy all his life—one may truly call that knowing men;

sentences.zh: 僕射為不亡矣！」

translations.literal: the Vice Director is not dead after all!"
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Director lives on after all!"

sentences.zh: 親舊見者為之流涕。

translations.literal: Relatives and old friends who saw it wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and old friends who saw it wept.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東鄉君卒，公私鹹謂貲財宜歸二女，田宅、僮役應屬弘微。

translations.literal: That year Lady Dongxiang died; in public and private all said the wealth should go to the two daughters, and the fields, houses, and servants should belong to Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lady Dongxiang died; everyone, in public and private, said the wealth should go to the two daughters and the fields, houses, and servants should belong to Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 弘微一無所取，自以私祿葬東鄉君。

translations.literal: Hongwei took nothing at all and buried Lady Dongxiang out of his private salary.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei took nothing at all and buried Lady Dongxiang out of his private salary.

sentences.zh: 混女夫殷睿好樗蒲，聞弘微不取財物，乃奪其妻妹及伯母、兩姑之分以還戲責。

translations.literal: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui was fond of gambling; hearing that Hongwei took none of the property, he seized the shares of his wife's younger sister, his wife's aunt, and his two sisters-in-law to pay off gambling debts.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui was fond of gambling; hearing that Hongwei took none of the property, he seized the shares belonging to his wife's younger sister, his wife's aunt, and his two sisters-in-law to pay off gambling debts.

sentences.zh: 內人皆化弘微之讓，一無所爭。

translations.literal: The women of the household were all moved by Hongwei's forbearance and contested nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The women of the household were all moved by Hongwei's forbearance and contested nothing.

sentences.zh: 或譏之曰：「謝氏累世財產，充殷君一朝戲責。

translations.literal: Someone mocked him, saying: "The Xie family's wealth accumulated over generations has gone to pay Lord Yin's gambling debts in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Someone mocked him, saying, "The Xie family's wealth accumulated over generations has gone to pay Lord Yin's gambling debts in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 理之不允，莫此為大。

translations.literal: Injustice could go no further than this.
translations.idiomatic: Injustice could go no further than this.

sentences.zh: 卿視而不言，譬棄物江海以為廉耳。

translations.literal: You watch and say nothing, as though casting goods into river and sea were called integrity.
translations.idiomatic: You watch and say nothing, as though casting goods into river and sea counted as integrity.

sentences.zh: 設使立清名而令家內不足，亦吾所不取也。」

translations.literal: Even if one establishes a pure name while leaving the household insufficient, that too is what I would not choose."
translations.idiomatic: Even if one establishes a pure reputation while leaving the household short, that too is what I would not choose."

sentences.zh: 弘微曰：「親戚爭財，為鄙之甚。

translations.literal: Hongwei said: "For kinsmen to quarrel over property is the height of vulgarity.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei said, "For kinsmen to quarrel over property is the height of vulgarity.

sentences.zh: 今內人尚能無言，豈可導之使爭乎！

translations.literal: Now the women of the household can still keep silent—how could I lead them to quarrel!
translations.idiomatic: Now the women of the household can still keep silent—how could I lead them to quarrel!

sentences.zh: 分多共少，不至有乏，身死之後，豈復見關也！」

translations.literal: Whether the shares are large or small, there will be no want; after I am dead, what will it matter to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Whether the shares are large or small, there will be no want; after I am dead, what will it matter to me!"

sentences.zh: 禿髮保周自涼奔魏，魏封保周為張掖公。

translations.literal: Tufa Baozhou fled from Liang to Wei, and Wei enfeoffed Baozhou as Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Baozhou fled from Liang to the Northern Wei, which enfeoffed him as Duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 魏李順復奉使至涼。

translations.literal: Li Shun of Wei again went on mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun of the Northern Wei again went on mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 涼王蒙遜遣中兵校郎楊定歸謂順曰：「年衰多疾，腰髀不隨，不堪拜伏；

translations.literal: The Liang king Mengsun sent the Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui to tell Shun: "I am aged and afflicted with many illnesses; my waist and thighs do not obey me, and I cannot bear to bow and prostrate;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang king Mengsun sent Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui to tell Shun, "I am aged and afflicted with many illnesses; my waist and thighs no longer obey me, and I cannot bear to bow and prostrate;

sentences.zh: 比三五日消息小差，當相見。」

translations.literal: in about three to five days, when my condition improves a little, I shall meet you."
translations.idiomatic: in about three to five days, when my condition improves a little, I shall meet you."

sentences.zh: 順曰：「王之老疾，朝廷所知；

translations.literal: Shun said: "Your Majesty's age and illness are known to the court;
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Your Majesty's age and illness are known to the court;

sentences.zh: 豈得自安，不見詔使！」

translations.literal: how can you rest at ease and refuse to see the imperial envoy!"
translations.idiomatic: how can you rest at ease and refuse to see the imperial envoy!"

sentences.zh: 明日，蒙遜延順入至庭中，蒙遜箕坐隱几，無動起之狀。

translations.literal: The next day Mengsun received Shun into the courtyard; Mengsun sat with legs spread, leaning on an armrest, with no sign of rising.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Mengsun received Shun into the courtyard; Mengsun sat with legs spread, leaning on a low armrest table, with no sign of rising.

sentences.zh: 順正色大言曰：「不謂此叟無禮乃至於此！

translations.literal: Shun, with stern countenance, spoke loudly: "I did not expect this old man to be so rude as this!
translations.idiomatic: Shun, with stern countenance, spoke loudly, "I did not expect this old man to be so rude as this!

sentences.zh: 今不憂覆而敢陵侮天地，魂魄逝矣，何用見之！」

translations.literal: Now, instead of fearing ruin, you dare insult Heaven and Earth; my spirit is already gone—what use is there in meeting you!"
translations.idiomatic: Now, instead of fearing ruin, you dare insult Heaven and Earth; my spirit is already gone—what use is there in meeting you!"

sentences.zh: 握節將出。

translations.literal: He grasped his staff of office and was about to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped his staff of office and was about to leave.

sentences.zh: 涼王使定歸追止之，曰：「太常既雅恕衰疾，傳聞朝廷有不拜之詔，是以敢自安耳。」

translations.literal: The Liang king sent Dinggui to run after him and stop him, saying: "The Grand Master of Ceremonies has graciously forgiven my aged illness; I heard that the court had issued an edict exempting me from bowing, and therefore I dared to rest at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang king sent Dinggui to run after him and stop him, saying, "The Grand Master of Ceremonies has graciously forgiven my aged illness; I heard that the court had issued an edict exempting me from bowing, and therefore I dared to rest at ease."

sentences.zh: 順曰：「齊桓公九合諸侯，一匡天下，周天下賜胙，命無下拜，桓公猶不敢失臣禮，下拜登受。

translations.literal: Shun said: "Duke Huan of Qi nine times assembled the feudal lords and once set the realm straight; when the Son of Heaven of Zhou granted sacrificial meat and ordered that he need not bow down, Huan still did not dare neglect the rites of a subject and descended the steps to bow and receive it on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Duke Huan of Qi nine times assembled the feudal lords and once set the realm straight; when the Son of Heaven of Zhou granted sacrificial meat and ordered that he need not bow down, Huan still did not dare neglect the rites of a subject and descended the steps to bow and receive it on the steps.

sentences.zh: 今王雖功高，未如齊桓；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's merit, though high, does not match Duke Huan of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's merit, though high, does not match Duke Huan of Qi;

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖相崇重，未有不拜之詔；

translations.literal: though the court honors you highly, there is no edict exempting you from bowing;
translations.idiomatic: though the court honors you highly, there is no edict exempting you from bowing;

sentences.zh: 而遽自偃蹇，此豈社稷之福邪！」

translations.literal: yet you abruptly put on arrogant airs—how can this be a blessing to the altars of soil and grain!"
translations.idiomatic: yet you abruptly put on arrogant airs—how can this be a blessing to the state!"

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃起，拜授詔。

translations.literal: Mengsun then rose, bowed, and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun then rose, bowed, and received the edict.

sentences.zh: 使還，魏主問以涼事。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the Wei ruler asked about affairs in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the Northern Wei emperor asked about affairs in Liang.

sentences.zh: 順曰：「蒙遜控制河右逾三十年，經涉艱難，粗識機變，綏集荒裔，群下畏服；

translations.literal: Shun said: "Mengsun has controlled the lands west of the Yellow River for more than thirty years; he has passed through hardship and roughly understands shifts in circumstance; he has pacified and gathered the remote frontiers, and his subordinates fear and obey him;
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Mengsun has controlled the lands west of the Yellow River for more than thirty years; he has passed through hardship and roughly understands shifts in circumstance; he has pacified and gathered the remote frontiers, and his subordinates fear and obey him;

sentences.zh: 雖不能貽厥孫謀，猶足以終其一世。

translations.literal: though he cannot bequeath plans to his descendants, he is still enough to finish out his own lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: though he cannot bequeath plans to his descendants, he is still enough to finish out his own lifetime.

sentences.zh: 然禮者德之輿，敬者身之基也；

translations.literal: Yet ritual is the carriage of virtue, and reverence is the foundation of the person;
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual is the carriage of virtue, and reverence is the foundation of the person;

sentences.zh: 蒙遜無禮，不敬，以臣觀之，不復年矣。」

translations.literal: Mengsun lacks ritual propriety and shows no reverence; in my view as your minister, he will not see out another year."
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun has cast off propriety and reverence; in my judgment, he will not live out the year."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「易世之後，何時當滅？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "After the change of generations, when will [Liang] be destroyed?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler said, "After he passes from the scene, when will the state fall?"

sentences.zh: 順曰：「蒙遜諸子，臣略見之，皆庸才也。

translations.literal: Shun said: "Of Mengsun's sons, I have seen them in passing—all are mediocre talents.
translations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "I have had some glimpse of Mengsun's sons, and they are all undistinguished men.

sentences.zh: 如聞敦煌太守牧犍，器性粗立，繼蒙遜者，必此人也。

translations.literal: As I have heard, the Governor of Dunhuang, Mujian, has capacity and character already roughly established; the one to succeed Mengsun will surely be this man.
translations.idiomatic: From what I hear, the Governor of Dunhuang, Mujian, already shows some measure of talent and character—the man who succeeds Mengsun will surely be he.

sentences.zh: 然比之於父，皆雲不及。

translations.literal: Yet compared with their father, all say they cannot measure up.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, everyone agrees that none of them equals their father.

sentences.zh: 此殆天之所以資聖明也。」

translations.literal: This is perhaps Heaven's way of aiding Your Sagely Illumination."
translations.idiomatic: This is surely Heaven's way of lending strength to Your Sagely Majesty."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「朕方有事東方，未暇西略。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "I am presently occupied with affairs in the east and have no leisure for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler said, "I am still engaged in the east and have no time to turn westward.

sentences.zh: 如卿所言，不過數年之外，不為晚也。」

translations.literal: As you say, it will be no more than a few years hence—not too late."
translations.idiomatic: As you say, a few years more will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 初，罽賓沙門曇無讖，自雲能使鬼治病，且有秘術。

translations.literal: Previously, the Gandharan monk Dharmaksema claimed he could use spirits to treat illness and possessed secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Gandharan monk Dharmaksema had claimed that he could summon spirits to heal the sick and that he possessed secret techniques.

sentences.zh: 涼王蒙遜甚重之，謂之「聖人」，諸女及子婦皆往受術。

translations.literal: The King of Liang Mengsun greatly valued him, calling him "the Sage"; all his daughters and daughters-in-law went to receive his teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang, Mengsun, held him in the highest esteem, called him "the Sage," and sent all his daughters and daughters-in-law to learn his arts.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，使李順往征之。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler heard of this, he sent Li Shun to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei ruler heard of this, he sent Li Shun to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜留不遣，仍殺之。

translations.literal: Mengsun detained him and would not send him forth, then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun kept him and refused to release him, then put him to death.

sentences.zh: 魏主由是怒涼。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was therefore angered at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler was enraged at Liang on this account.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜荒淫猜虐，群下苦之。

translations.literal: Mengsun was dissolute, suspicious, and cruel; his subordinates suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun was debauched, suspicious, and cruel, and his officials and people groaned under his rule.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之下元嘉十年（

translations.literal: The lower part of "Emperor Wen of the Ancestor [dynasty], Part One" — Yuanjia year 10 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, Part One (continued) — Yuanjia year 10 (

sentences.zh: 癸酉，公元四三三年）

translations.literal: guiyou, corresponding to 433 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guiyou, corresponding to 433 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，魏主遣永昌王健督諸軍救遼西。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yimao, the Wei ruler dispatched Yongchang Wang Jian to supervise the various armies in relieving Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on yimao, the first day of the first month, the Wei ruler sent Prince Yongchang Jian to command the armies sent to relieve Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 己未，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏以樂安王范為都督秦、雍等五州諸軍事、衛大將軍、開府儀同三司、長安鎮都大將。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Wei appointed Prince of Le'an Fan as Supervisor of Military Affairs for the five provinces including Qin and Yong, Grand General of the Guard, Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, and Commander-in-Chief of the Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Wei appointed Prince Le'an Fan supervisor of military affairs for Qin, Yong, and three other provinces, Grand General of the Guard, Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, and commander-in-chief of the Chang'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 魏主以范年少，更選舊德平西將軍崔徽、征北大將軍雁門張黎為之副，共鎮長安。

translations.literal: Because the Wei ruler considered Fan young, he further selected the veteran worthy, the General Who Pacifies the West Cui Hui, and the General Who Conquers the North Zhang Li of Yanmen as his deputies, together to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Fan still young, the Wei ruler also chose the seasoned General Who Pacifies the West Cui Hui and the General Who Conquers the North Zhang Li of Yanmen as his deputies, and together they guarded Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 徽，宏之弟也。

translations.literal: Hui was the younger brother of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the younger brother of Hong.

sentences.zh: 范廉恭寬惠，徽務敦大體，黎清約公平，政刑簡易，輕徭薄賦，關中遂安。

translations.literal: Fan was incorrupt, respectful, generous, and kind; Hui devoted himself to the larger principles of governance; Li was austere, fair, and equitable. Government and punishments were kept simple; corvée and taxes were lightened; and the Guanzhong region thereafter knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was upright, respectful, generous, and humane; Hui focused on the broad principles of rule; Li was frugal, fair, and even-handed. Administration and punishments were kept simple, corvée and taxes were reduced, and Guanzhong soon settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，魏主以馮崇為都督幽、平、東夷諸軍事、車騎大將軍、幽、平二州牧，封遼西王，隸其國尚書事，食遼西十郡，承製假授尚書、刺史、征虜已下官。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu, the Wei ruler appointed Feng Chong as Supervisor of Military Affairs for You, Ping, and the Eastern Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of You and Ping provinces, enfeoffed him as Prince of Liaoxi, placed him under the jurisdiction of his state's Secretariat, granted him revenues from ten commanderies of Liaoxi, and authorized him by imperial rescript to provisionally appoint officials from Secretariat members and inspectors down to those bearing the title General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu, the Wei ruler made Feng Chong supervisor of military affairs for You, Ping, and the Eastern Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and governor of You and Ping; enfeoffed him as Prince of Liaoxi; assigned him to the secretariat of his own state; granted him the revenues of ten Liaoxi commanderies; and authorized him by imperial rescript to appoint, on a provisional basis, all officials from secretariat members and provincial inspectors down to the rank of General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 魏平涼休屠征西將軍金崖、羌涇州刺史狄子玉與安定鎮將延普爭權，崖、子玉舉兵攻普，不克，退保胡空谷。

translations.literal: Jin Ya, the General Who Conquers the West of the Xiutu people in Wei-administered Liang, and Di Ziyu, the Qiang Governor of Jingzhou, vied for power with Yan Pu, the garrison commander of Anding. Ya and Ziyu raised troops to attack Pu but failed to overcome him and withdrew to hold Hukong Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei pacification of Liang, the Xiutu General Who Conquers the West Jin Ya and the Qiang governor of Jingzhou Di Ziyu struggled for power with Yan Pu, the garrison commander of Anding. Ya and Ziyu raised troops to attack Pu, failed to prevail, and withdrew to defend Hukong Valley.

sentences.zh: 魏主以虎牢鎮大將陸俟為安定鎮大將，擊崖等，皆擒之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler appointed Lu Si, the garrison commander of Hulao, as garrison commander of Anding and attacked Ya and the others, capturing them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler appointed Lu Si, commander of the Hulao garrison, commander of the Anding garrison, attacked Ya and his allies, and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 魏主征陸俟為散騎常侍，出為懷荒鎮大將，未期歲，高車諸莫弗訟俟嚴急無恩，復請前鎮將郎孤。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler summoned Lu Si and appointed him Attendant Cavalier at Large, then sent him out as garrison commander of Huaihuang. Before a full year had passed, the zhimo-fu of the Gaoche people complained that Si was severe, harsh, and devoid of kindness, and again requested the former garrison commander Lang Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler recalled Lu Si to court as Attendant Cavalier at Large, then sent him out as commander of the Huaihuang garrison. Before a year was out, the zhimo-fu of the Gaoche lodged complaints that Si was harsh and merciless, and asked that the former garrison commander Lang Gu be restored.

sentences.zh: 魏主征俟還，以孤代之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler recalled Si and replaced him with Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler recalled Si and sent Lang Gu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 俟既至，言於帝曰：「不過期年，郎孤必敗，高車必叛。」

translations.literal: When Si arrived, he said to the Emperor: "In no more than a year Lang Gu will fail, and the Gaoche will rebel."
translations.idiomatic: When Si reached court, he told the Emperor, "Within a year Lang Gu will fail, and the Gaoche will rebel."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責之，使以建業公歸第。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered, harshly rebuked him, and sent him home under his title of Duke of Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious, rebuked him sharply, and sent him home to his estate as Duke of Jianye.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸莫弗果殺郎孤而叛。

translations.literal: The next year, the zhimo-fu indeed killed Lang Gu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the zhimo-fu did indeed kill Lang Gu and rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，立召俟問之曰：「卿何以知其然也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and immediately summoned Si, asking: "How did you know it would happen thus?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and at once summoned Si, asking, "How did you know that this would happen?"

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「高車不知上下之禮，故臣臨之以威，制之以法，欲以漸訓導，使知分限。

translations.literal: Si said: "The Gaoche do not understand the proprieties of superior and inferior, so I confronted them with authority and restrained them with law, intending to train and guide them gradually so they would learn their proper bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "The Gaoche do not understand the proprieties of superior and inferior. I therefore met them with authority and restrained them with law, hoping by degrees to train and guide them so they would learn their proper limits.

sentences.zh: 而諸莫弗惡臣所為，訟臣無恩，稱孤之美。

translations.literal: But the zhimo-fu resented what I did, complained that I had no kindness, and praised Gu's merits.
translations.idiomatic: But the zhimo-fu resented my conduct, accused me of lacking kindness, and praised Lang Gu.

sentences.zh: 臣以罪去，孤獲還鎮，悅其稱譽，益收名聲，專用寬恕待之。

translations.literal: I departed under accusation, Gu returned to the garrison, delighted at their praise, and sought all the more to win reputation by treating them exclusively with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: I left under censure; Lang Gu returned to the garrison, pleased by their praise, and sought all the more to win a name for himself by treating them only with indulgence.

sentences.zh: 無禮之人，易生驕慢，不過期年，無復上下，孤所不堪，必將復以法裁之。

translations.literal: People without propriety easily become arrogant and insolent. In less than a year there would no longer be any distinction of superior and inferior; what Gu could not endure, he would surely again restrain with law.
translations.idiomatic: Men without propriety easily grow arrogant. In less than a year there would no longer be any distinction of superior and inferior; what Lang Gu could not bear, he would surely try to curb again with law.

sentences.zh: 如此，則眾心怨懟，必生禍亂矣。」

translations.literal: In this way popular sentiment would turn resentful and rebellious, and calamity and disorder would inevitably arise."
translations.idiomatic: When that happened, popular resentment would boil over and disaster would follow."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿身雖短，思慮何長也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Though your person is short, how far your thinking reaches!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "Your body may be short, but your foresight runs long!"

sentences.zh: 即日復以為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: That very day he reappointed him Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he restored him to the post of Attendant Cavalier at Large.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏主如河西，遣兼散騎常侍宋宣來聘，且為太子晃求婚；

translations.literal: On renwu, the Wei ruler went to Hexi and dispatched the concurrent Attendant Cavalier at Large Song Xuan on a mission of courtesy, also to seek a marriage alliance for Crown Prince Huang;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Wei ruler went to Hexi and sent the concurrent Attendant Cavalier at Large Song Xuan on a diplomatic mission, also to seek a bride for Crown Prince Huang;

sentences.zh: 帝依違答之。

translations.literal: The Emperor answered evasively and without commitment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered evasively, neither accepting nor refusing.

sentences.zh: 劉道濟卒，梁俊之、裴方明等密埋其屍於齋後，詐為道濟教命以答簽疏，雖其母、妻亦不知也。

translations.literal: Liu Daoji died. Liang Junzhi, Pei Fangming, and others secretly buried his corpse behind the study and forged orders in Daoji's name to answer official correspondence—even his mother and wife did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoji died. Liang Junzhi, Pei Fangming, and the others secretly buried his body behind the study and forged orders in Daoji's name to answer official documents; not even his mother and wife knew.

sentences.zh: 程道養於毀金橋登壇郊天，方明將三千人出擊之，道養等大敗，退保廣漢。

translations.literal: Cheng Daoyang ascended an altar at the destroyed Jin Bridge to perform suburban sacrifices to Heaven. Fangming led three thousand men out to attack him. Daoyang and his followers were heavily defeated and withdrew to hold Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Daoyang mounted an altar at the ruined Jin Bridge to perform the suburban sacrifice to Heaven. Fangming led three thousand men against him, routed Daoyang's forces, and drove them back to Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史臨川王義慶以巴東太守周籍之督巴西等五郡諸軍事，將二千人救成都。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou, Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, dispatched the Governor of Badong Zhou Jizhi to supervise military affairs for the five commanderies including Baxi, leading two thousand men to relieve Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Jingzhou, Prince Linchuan Yiqing, sent the governor of Badong Zhou Jizhi to take command of military affairs in Baxi and four other commanderies, and led two thousand men to relieve Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 三月，亡人司馬天助降於魏，自稱晉會稽世子元顯之子；

translations.literal: In the third month, the fugitive Sima Tianzhu surrendered to Wei, claiming to be the son of Jin's heir apparent to Kuaiji, Yuanxian;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the fugitive Sima Tianzhu surrendered to Wei, claiming to be the son of Jin heir apparent Yuanxian of Kuaiji;

sentences.zh: 魏人以為青、徐二州刺史、東海公。

translations.literal: The Wei appointed him Inspector of Qing and Xu provinces and Duke of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed him inspector of Qing and Xu and Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On renzi, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 趙廣等自廣漢至郫，連營百數。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang and others, from Guanghan to Pi, established camps numbering in the hundreds in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang and his allies strung together scores of camps from Guanghan to Pi.

sentences.zh: 周籍之與裴方明等合兵攻郫，克之，進擊廣等於廣漢，廣等走還涪及五城。

translations.literal: Zhou Jizhi joined forces with Pei Fangming and others to attack Pi, took it, then pressed the attack on Guang and the others at Guanghan. Guang and the others fled back to Fu and Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jizhi joined Pei Fangming and the others, attacked Pi and took it, then pressed Zhao Guang and his men at Guanghan until they fled back to Fu and Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅，始發劉道濟喪。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuyin, Liu Daoji's funeral procession finally set out.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuyin, Liu Daoji's funeral procession was at last sent forth.

sentences.zh: 帝聞梁、南秦二州刺史甄法護刑政不治，失氐、羌之和，乃自徒中起蕭思話為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Zhen Fahu, Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, was mismanaging punishments and government and had lost the goodwill of the Di and Qiang peoples. He therefore raised Xiao Sihua from among the convicts to be Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhen Fahu, inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, was governing badly and had lost the goodwill of the Di and Qiang, the Emperor raised Xiao Sihua from among the convicts and made him inspector of the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 法護，法崇之兄也。

translations.literal: Fahu was the elder brother of Fachong.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was the elder brother of Fachong.

sentences.zh: 涼王蒙遜病甚，國人共議，以世子菩提幼弱，立菩提之兄敦煌太守牧犍為世子，加中外都督、大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The King of Liang Mengsun was gravely ill. The people of the state deliberated together and, because the heir apparent Puti was young and weak, installed Puti's elder brother, the Governor of Dunhuang Mujian, as heir apparent, adding the titles Supervisor of Internal and External Affairs, Grand General, and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang Mengsun fell gravely ill. The people of the state debated the succession and, because the heir apparent Puti was young and weak, set up Puti's elder brother Mujian, governor of Dunhuang, as heir apparent, with the added titles of supervisor of internal and external affairs, grand general, and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜卒，謚曰武宣王，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: Mengsun died; his posthumous title was King Wuxuan, and his temple name was Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun died and was posthumously titled King Wuxuan, with the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 牧犍即河西王位，大赦，改元永和，立子封壇為世子，加撫軍大將軍、錄尚書事，遣使請命於魏。

translations.literal: Mujian succeeded to the kingship of Hexi, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Yonghe, installed his son Fengtan as heir apparent with the added titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Secretariat, and dispatched envoys to request investiture from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian took the throne of Hexi, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Yonghe, made his son Fengtan heir apparent with the added titles of General Who Pacifies the Army and director of the secretariat, and sent envoys to Wei to request formal recognition.

sentences.zh: 牧犍聰穎好學，和雅有度量，故國人立之。

translations.literal: Mujian was intelligent, fond of learning, gentle, refined, and broad-minded, and for this reason the people of the state chose him.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian was bright, studious, gentle, and magnanimous, and for that reason the people had chosen him.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏主遣李順迎武宣王女為夫人。

translations.literal: Previously the Wei ruler had sent Li Shun to welcome King Wuxuan's daughter as his consort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Wei ruler had sent Li Shun to fetch King Wuxuan's daughter as his consort.

sentences.zh: 會卒，牧犍稱先王遺意，遣左丞宋繇送其妹興平公主於魏，拜右昭儀。

translations.literal: Just then [Mengsun] died. Mujian, citing his late father's wishes, sent the Left Chancellor Song Yao to escort his younger sister, Princess Xingping, to Wei, where she was appointed Right Lady of Bright Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Mengsun died. Mujian, citing his late father's wishes, sent the Left Chancellor Song Yao to escort his younger sister Princess Xingping to Wei, where she was made Right Lady of Bright Deportment.

sentences.zh: 魏主謂李順曰：「卿言蒙遜死，今則驗矣；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said to Li Shun: "You said Mengsun would die—and now it has been verified;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler said to Li Shun, "You said Mengsun would die, and now it has come true;

sentences.zh: 又言牧犍立，何其妙哉！

translations.literal: you also said Mujian would succeed—how splendidly accurate!
translations.idiomatic: you also said Mujian would succeed—how keen your judgment!

sentences.zh: 朕克涼州，亦當不遠。」

translations.literal: My conquest of Liangzhou cannot be far off."
translations.idiomatic: My conquest of Liangzhou cannot be far away."

sentences.zh: 於是賜絹千匹，廄馬一乘，進號安西將軍，寵待彌厚，政事無鉅細，皆與之參議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted him a thousand bolts of silk, one stable horse, promoted him to General Who Pacifies the West, lavished favor upon him ever more generously, and consulted with him on every matter of government, great and small.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he granted him a thousand bolts of silk and one stable horse, promoted him to General Who Pacifies the West, treated him with ever greater favor, and consulted him on every matter of state, great or small.

sentences.zh: 遣順拜牧犍都督涼沙河三州、西域羌戎諸軍事、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、涼州刺史、河西王，以宋繇為河西王右相。

translations.literal: He sent Shun to invest Mujian as Supervisor of Military Affairs for Liang, Sha, and He provinces, the Western Regions, and the Qiang and Rong peoples; General of Chariots and Cavalry; Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes; Inspector of Liang; and King of Hexi; and appointed Song Yao as the Right Chancellor to the King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shun to invest Mujian as supervisor of military affairs for Liang, Sha, and He, the Western Regions, and the Qiang and Rong; General of Chariots and Cavalry; Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes; inspector of Liang; and King of Hexi, and appointed Song Yao right chancellor to the King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 牧犍以無功受賞，留順，上表乞安、平一號；

translations.literal: Mujian, feeling he had received rewards without merit, detained Shun and submitted a memorial requesting a title such as "An" or "Ping";
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he had been rewarded without merit, Mujian detained Shun and memorialized the throne asking for a title bearing the character An or Ping;

sentences.zh: 優詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict of gracious response did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 牧犍尊敦煌劉昺為國師，親拜之，命官屬以下皆北面受業。

translations.literal: Mujian honored Liu Bing of Dunhuang as State Master, bowed to him in person, and ordered all officials and subordinates to face north and receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian honored Liu Bing of Dunhuang as state master, bowed to him in person, and ordered all officials and subordinates to face north and receive instruction from him.

sentences.zh: 五月，己亥，魏主如山北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jihai, the Wei ruler went to the north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jihai, the Wei ruler went north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范陽邁遣使入貢，求領交州；

translations.literal: Fan Yangmai, King of Linyi, dispatched envoys to present tribute and request to be granted authority over Jiaozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yangmai, king of Linyi, sent envoys with tribute and asked to be put in charge of Jiaozhou;

sentences.zh: 詔答以道遠，不許。

translations.literal: An edict replied that the distance was too great and denied the request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that the distance was too great and refused.

sentences.zh: 裴方明進軍向涪城，破張尋、唐頻、擒程道助，斬嚴遐，於是趙廣等皆奔散。

translations.literal: Pei Fangming advanced toward Fucheng, defeated Zhang Xun and Tang Pin, captured Cheng Daozhu, beheaded Yan Xia, and thereupon Zhao Guang and the others all fled and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Fangming marched on Fucheng, defeated Zhang Xun and Tang Pin, captured Cheng Daozhu, beheaded Yan Xia, and Zhao Guang and the rest broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏永昌王健、左僕射安原督諸軍擊和龍，將軍樓孛文別將五千騎圍凡城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Wei Prince of Yongchang Jian and Left Vice Director An Yuan supervised the various armies in an attack on Helong; the general Lou Beiwen separately commanded five thousand cavalry to besiege Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Prince Yongchang Jian of Wei and Left Vice Director An Yuan commanded the armies against Helong, while General Lou Beiwen led five thousand cavalry in a separate force to besiege Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 燕守將封羽以凡城降，收其三千餘家而還。

translations.literal: Yan's garrison commander Feng Yu surrendered Fancheng; [the Wei forces] gathered more than three thousand families and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's garrison commander Feng Yu surrendered Fancheng; the Wei forces took more than three thousand households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏人發秦、雍兵一萬，築小城於長安城內。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Wei mobilized ten thousand troops from Qin and Yong and built a small city within Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Wei mobilized ten thousand troops from Qin and Yong and built a small inner citadel within Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，馮崇上表請說降其父，魏主不聽。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Feng Chong submitted a memorial requesting permission to persuade his father to surrender; the Wei ruler did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Feng Chong memorialized asking leave to persuade his father to surrender; the Wei ruler refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，益州刺史甄法崇至成都，收費謙，誅之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Inspector of Yizhou Zhen Fachong reached Chengdu, arrested Fei Qian, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the inspector of Yizhou Zhen Fachong reached Chengdu, arrested Fei Qian, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 程道養、張尋將二千餘家逃入郪山，餘黨各擁眾藏竄山谷，時出為寇不絕。

translations.literal: Cheng Daoyang and Zhang Xun led more than two thousand families in flight into Mount Pi; the remaining partisans each gathered bands and hid in mountain valleys, emerging from time to time to raid without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Daoyang and Zhang Xun fled into Mount Pi with more than two thousand households; the remaining rebels gathered bands and hid in the mountains, raiding from time to time without end.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏主遣兼大鴻臚崔賾持節，拜氐王相難當為征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、秦、梁二州牧、南秦王。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Wei ruler dispatched the concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Ze bearing credentials to invest the Di king Yang Nandang as General Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, Governor of Qin and Liang provinces, and King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Wei ruler sent the concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Ze with credentials to invest the Di king Yang Nandang as General Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, governor of Qin and Liang, and King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 賾，逞之子。

translations.literal: Ze was the son of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was the son of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 楊難當因蕭思話未至，甄法護將下，舉兵襲梁州，破白馬，獲晉昌太守張范，敗法護參軍魯安期等；

translations.literal: Yang Nandang, because Xiao Sihua had not yet arrived and Zhen Fahu's troops were demoralized, raised troops and raided Liangzhou. He took Baima, captured the Governor of Jinchang Zhang Fan, and defeated Fahu's staff officer Lu Anqi and others;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang, taking advantage of Xiao Sihua's absence and the low morale of Zhen Fahu's troops, raised an army and struck Liangzhou. He took Baima, captured the governor of Jinchang Zhang Fan, and defeated Fahu's staff officer Lu Anqi and others;

sentences.zh: 又攻葭萌，獲晉壽太守范延郎。

translations.literal: He also attacked Jiameng and captured the Governor of Jinshou Fan Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Jiameng and captured the governor of Jinshou Fan Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丁未，法護棄城奔洋川之西城。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on dingwei, Fahu abandoned the city and fled to the western citadel of Yangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on dingwei, Fahu abandoned the city and fled to the western citadel of Yangchuan.

sentences.zh: 難當遂有漢中之地，以其司馬趙溫為梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Nandang thereby came to hold the lands of Hanzhong and appointed his Marshal Zhao Wen as Inspector of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang thereby held Hanzhong and appointed his marshal Zhao Wen inspector of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jisi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主如陰山之北。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Wei ruler went to the north of the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Wei ruler went north of the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 魏寧朔將軍盧玄來聘。

translations.literal: The Wei General of Pacifying the North Lu Xuan came on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan, General of Pacifying the North of Wei, came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 前秘書監謝靈運，好為山澤之遊，窮幽極險。

translations.literal: The former Director of the Secretariat Xie Lingyun delighted in roaming mountains and marshes, pushing to the remotest depths and the most perilous extremes.
translations.idiomatic: The former director of the secretariat Xie Lingyun loved to roam mountains and wild country, seeking out the deepest recesses and the steepest peril.

sentences.zh: 從者數百人，伐木開徑；

translations.literal: His followers numbered in the hundreds; they felled trees to open paths;
translations.idiomatic: He went with several hundred followers, felling trees to cut paths;

sentences.zh: 百姓驚擾，以為山賊。

translations.literal: the common people were alarmed and disturbed, believing them to be mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: and the local people were thrown into alarm, taking them for mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守孟顗與靈運有隙，表其有異志，發兵自防。

translations.literal: The Governor of Kuaiji Meng Yi bore a grudge against Lingyun and memorialized the throne that Lingyun harbored rebellious intent, then mobilized troops to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Kuaiji Meng Yi, who bore a grudge against Lingyun, memorialized that Lingyun harbored rebellious intent and mobilized troops to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 靈運詣自陳，上以為臨川內史。

translations.literal: Lingyun went to court to explain himself; the Emperor appointed him Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun went to court to explain himself, and the Emperor made him administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 靈運游放自若，廢棄郡事，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: Lingyun wandered freely as before, neglecting the affairs of the commandery, and was impeached by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun wandered as freely as before, neglected the affairs of the commandery, and was impeached by the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲，司徒遣使隨州從事鄭望生收靈運；

translations.literal: That year the Minister over the Masses dispatched an envoy; the staff officer of Suizhou, Zheng Wangsheng, was sent to take Lingyun into custody;
translations.idiomatic: That year the Minister over the Masses sent an envoy, and Zheng Wangsheng, a staff officer of Suizhou, was dispatched to take Lingyun into custody;

sentences.zh: 靈運執望生，興兵逃逸，作詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連恥。」

translations.literal: Lingyun seized Wangsheng, raised troops, and fled. He composed a poem: "When Han fell, Zifang rose up; when Qin ruled, Lu Lian felt shame."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun seized Wangsheng, raised troops, and fled, composing a poem: "When Han perished, Zifang rose in wrath; when Qin ruled, Lu Lian knew shame."

sentences.zh: 追討，擒之。

translations.literal: Pursuers overtook him and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers overtook him and captured him.

sentences.zh: 廷尉奏靈運帥眾反叛，論正斬刑。

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice reported that Lingyun had led a crowd in rebellion and recommended execution according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of justice reported that Lingyun had led men in rebellion and recommended death by decapitation under the statute.

sentences.zh: 上愛其才，欲免官而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor, cherishing his talent, wished only to dismiss him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, cherishing his talent, wished only to dismiss him from office.

sentences.zh: 袁城王義康堅執，謂不恕。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang insisted firmly, saying he should not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Yikang held firm and said he should not be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 乃降死一等，徙廣州。

translations.literal: He was therefore reduced one degree from death and exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sentenced one degree below death and exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，或告靈運令人買兵器，結健兒，欲於三江口篡取之，不果。

translations.literal: After a long while, someone reported that Lingyun had sent men to buy weapons and recruited strong youths, intending to seize him at Sanjiangkou—but the plan did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, someone reported that Lingyun had sent men to buy weapons and recruited strong youths, intending to seize him at Sanjiangkou, but the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 詔於廣州棄市。

translations.literal: An edict ordered execution by public display in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him executed in the marketplace at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 靈運恃才放逸，多所陵忽，故及於禍。

translations.literal: Lingyun relied on his talent, was unrestrained and dissolute, and treated many with contempt and disregard; therefore he brought calamity upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun leaned on his talent, lived without restraint, and treated many with contempt—thus he brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 魏立徐州於外黃，以刁雍為刺史。

translations.literal: Wei established Xuzhou at Waihuang, appointing Diao Yong as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei established Xuzhou at Waihuang and appointed Diao Yong its inspector.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之下元嘉十一年（

translations.literal: The lower part of "Emperor Wen of the Ancestor [dynasty], Part One" — Yuanjia year 11 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, Part One (continued) — Yuanjia year 11 (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元四三四年）

translations.literal: jiaxu, corresponding to 434 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiaxu, corresponding to 434 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊戌，燕王遣使請和於魏，魏主不許。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wuxu, the Yan king sent envoys to sue for peace with Wei; the Wei ruler did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on wuxu of the first month, the Yan king sent envoys to sue for peace with the Northern Wei, but the Wei ruler refused.

sentences.zh: 楊難當以克漢中告捷於魏，送雍州流民七千家於長安。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang reported his victory in taking Hanzhong to Wei and sent seven thousand families of displaced persons from Yongzhou to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang reported his conquest of Hanzhong to the Northern Wei and sent seven thousand refugee families from Yongzhou to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話至襄陽，遣橫野司馬蕭承之為前驅。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua reached Xiangyang and dispatched the marshal of the General of Roaming Wilds, Xiao Chengzhi, as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua reached Xiangyang and sent Xiao Chengzhi, marshal under the General of Roaming Wilds, ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 承之緣道收兵，得千人，進據磝頭。

translations.literal: Chengzhi gathered troops along the route, obtaining a thousand men, and advanced to seize Qiaotou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi gathered troops along the march, mustered a thousand men, and advanced to take Qiaotou.

sentences.zh: 楊難當焚掠漢中，引眾西還，留趙溫守梁州；

translations.literal: Yang Nandang burned and plundered Hanzhong, led his forces westward in retreat, and left Zhao Wen to hold Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang burned and plundered Hanzhong, then withdrew west with his army, leaving Zhao Wen to hold Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 又遣其魏興太守薛健據黃金山。

translations.literal: He also sent his Administrator of Weixing, Xue Jian, to hold Huangjinshan.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his administrator of Weixing, Xue Jian, to hold Huangjinshan.

sentences.zh: 思話遣陰平太守蕭坦攻鐵城戍，拔之。

translations.literal: Sihua dispatched the Administrator of Yinping, Xiao Tan, to attack Tiechenggu and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua sent the administrator of Yinping, Xiao Tan, to attack the garrison at Tiecheng and took it.

sentences.zh: 二月，趙溫、薛健與其馮翊太守蒲甲子合攻坦營，坦擊破之，溫等退保西水。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhao Wen, Xue Jian, and their Administrator of Fengyi, Pu Jiazi, jointly attacked Tan's camp; Tan routed them, and Wen and the others fell back to defend Xishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Zhao Wen, Xue Jian, and their administrator of Fengyi, Pu Jiazi, jointly attacked Tan's camp. Tan routed them, and Wen and his allies withdrew to hold Xishui.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶遣龍驤將軍裴方明將三千人助承之，拔黃金戍而據之。

translations.literal: Prince of Linchuan Yiqing sent the General of the Flying Dragon Pei Fangming with three thousand men to assist Chengzhi; they captured Huangjinggu and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linchuan Yiqing sent General of the Flying Dragon Pei Fangming with three thousand men to aid Chengzhi. They captured the Huangjin garrison and held it.

sentences.zh: 溫棄州城，退據小城，健、甲子退保下桃城。

translations.literal: Wen abandoned the provincial city and withdrew to a smaller one; Jian and Jiazi fell back to defend Xiataocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wen abandoned the provincial seat and withdrew to a smaller city, while Jian and Jiazi fell back to hold Xiataocheng.

sentences.zh: 思話繼至，與承之共擊趙溫等，屢破之。

translations.literal: Sihua arrived afterward and, together with Chengzhi, repeatedly defeated Zhao Wen and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua arrived in turn and, joining Chengzhi, repeatedly defeated Zhao Wen and his allies.

sentences.zh: 行參軍王靈濟別將出洋川，攻南城，拔之，擒其守將趙英。

translations.literal: The acting staff officer Wang Lingji led a separate column out through Yangchuan, attacked Nancheng, captured it, and seized its defending general Zhao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The acting staff officer Wang Lingji led a separate force out through Yangchuan, attacked Nancheng, took it, and captured its defending general Zhao Ying.

sentences.zh: 南城空無所資，靈濟引兵還，與承之合。

translations.literal: Nancheng was empty and offered no supplies; Lingji led his troops back and joined Chengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng was empty and offered no supplies, so Lingji withdrew and rejoined Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 魏主以西海公主妻柔然敕連可汗，又納其妹為夫人，遣穎川王提往逆之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler gave the Princess of the Western Sea in marriage to the Rouran khan Chilian, and also took Chilian's younger sister as his consort; he sent Prince of Yingchuan Ti to go and meet her.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler gave the Princess of the Western Sea in marriage to the Rouran khan Chilian and also took Chilian's younger sister as consort, dispatching Prince Yingchuan Ti to meet her on the road.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，敕連遣其異母兄禿鹿傀送妹，並獻馬二千匹。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Chilian sent his elder half-brother Tulu Kui to escort his sister, and also presented two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Chilian sent his elder half-brother Tulu Kui to escort his sister and presented two thousand horses as well.

sentences.zh: 魏主以其妹為左昭儀。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler made Chilian's younger sister Left Lady of Brilliant Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler made Chilian's younger sister Left Lady of Brilliant Beauty.

sentences.zh: 提，曜之子也。

translations.literal: Ti was the son of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was the son of Yao.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏主還宮；

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Wei ruler returned to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the Wei ruler returned to the palace;

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，復如河西。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, he again went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, he again set out for Hexi.

sentences.zh: 楊難當遣其子和將兵與蒲甲子等共擊蕭承之，相拒四十餘日，圍承之數十重，短兵接，弓矢無所復施。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang sent his son He with troops to join Pu Jiazi and others in attacking Xiao Chengzhi; they faced one another for more than forty days, surrounding Chengzhi in dozens of rings of siege; fighting at close quarters, bows and arrows could no longer be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang sent his son He with troops to join Pu Jiazi and others in attacking Xiao Chengzhi. For more than forty days the two sides faced off, Chengzhi ringed by dozens of encircling lines. Fighting closed to hand strokes, neither side could any longer use bow or arrow.

sentences.zh: 氐悉衣犀甲，戈矛所不能入。

translations.literal: The Di all wore rhinoceros-hide armor, into which spears and halberds could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Di all wore rhinoceros-hide armor that spears and halberds could not pierce.

sentences.zh: 承之斷槊長數尺，以大斧椎之，一槊輒貫數人。

translations.literal: Chengzhi cut his spears to several feet in length, drove them in with a great axe, and each spear thrust would pierce several men.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi cut his spears down to several feet, drove them home with a great axe, and each thrust ran through several men.

sentences.zh: 氐不能當，燒營走，據大桃。

translations.literal: The Di could not withstand him; they burned their camp and fled, holding out at Datao.
translations.idiomatic: The Di could not stand against him. They burned their camp and fled, making a stand at Datao.

sentences.zh: 閏月，承之等追擊之，至南城，氐敗走，斬獲甚眾，悉收漢中故地，置戍於葭萌水。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Chengzhi and the others pursued them to Nancheng; the Di were defeated and fled, and very many were killed or captured. They fully recovered the former lands of Hanzhong and established garrisons at Jiamengshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Chengzhi and his men pursued them to Nancheng. The Di were routed and fled; the dead and captured were very many. They recovered all the former territory of Hanzhong and established garrisons at Jiamengshui.

sentences.zh: 初，桓希既敗，氐王楊盛據漢中，梁州刺史范元之、傅歆皆治魏興，唯得魏興、上庸、新城三郡。

translations.literal: Initially, after Huan Xi was defeated, the Di king Yang Sheng held Hanzhong, while the inspectors of Liangzhou Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin both administered from Weixing, holding only the three commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Huan Xi was defeated, the Di king Yang Sheng held Hanzhong, while the Liangzhou inspectors Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin both governed from Weixing and controlled only the three commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 及索邈為刺史，乃治南城。

translations.literal: When Suo Miao became inspector, the seat was moved to Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Suo Miao became inspector, the seat was moved to Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 至是，南城為氐所焚，不可復固，蕭思話徙鎮南鄭。

translations.literal: At this time Nancheng had been burned by the Di and could no longer be held; Xiao Sihua moved his headquarters to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: By now Nancheng had been burned by the Di and could no longer be held, so Xiao Sihua moved his headquarters to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，赫連昌叛魏西走；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Helian Chang rebelled against Wei and fled westward;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Helian Chang rebelled against the Northern Wei and fled west;

sentences.zh: 丙子，河西候將格殺之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, a frontier patrol officer in Hexi intercepted and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, a frontier patrol officer in Hexi intercepted and killed him.

sentences.zh: 魏人並其群弟誅之。

translations.literal: The Wei people executed him and his brothers together.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei then executed him and all his brothers together.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，燕王遣尚書高顒上表稱籓，請罪於魏，乞以季女充掖庭；

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Yan king sent the Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial professing vassalage, begging pardon from Wei, and asking that his youngest daughter be sent to fill the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Yan king sent Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial professing vassalage, begging pardon from the Northern Wei and asking that his youngest daughter be sent to the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 魏主乃許之，征其太子王仁入朝。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler thereupon agreed and summoned his crown prince Wang Ren to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler agreed and summoned his crown prince Wang Ren to court.

sentences.zh: 燕王送魏使者於什門還平城。

translations.literal: The Yan king sent back the Wei envoy Yu Shenmen to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king sent the Wei envoy Yu Shenmen back to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 什門在燕二十一年，不屈節。

translations.literal: Shenmen had spent twenty-one years in Yan without yielding in fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: Shenmen had spent twenty-one years in Yan without ever yielding his integrity.

sentences.zh: 魏主下詔褒稱，以比蘇武，拜治書御史，賜羊千口，帛千匹，策告宗廟，頒示天下。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler issued an edict praising him, comparing him to Su Wu; he was appointed Imperial Censor and granted a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk; an announcement was made to the ancestral temple and displayed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler issued an edict praising him and comparing him to Su Wu. Shenmen was appointed imperial censor and granted a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk; the court reported the honor to the ancestral temple and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 戊子，休屠金當川圍魏陰密。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Xiutu chieftain Jin Dangchuan besieged Wei's Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the Xiutu chieftain Jin Dangchuan besieged the Northern Wei city of Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，魏徵西大將軍常山王素擊之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, the Northern Wei Grand General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Changshan Su, attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, the Northern Wei Grand General Who Conquers the West, Prince Changshan Su, attacked him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主行如河西。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Wei ruler set out for Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the Wei ruler set out for Hexi.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，獲當川，斬之。

translations.literal: On renxu, they captured Dangchuan and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, they captured Dangchuan and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 甄法護坐委鎮，賜死於獄。

translations.literal: Zhen Fahu was convicted of abandoning his post and was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Fahu was convicted of abandoning his post and was granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 楊難當遣使奉表謝罪，帝下詔赦之。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang sent envoys with a memorial begging forgiveness; the Emperor issued an edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang sent envoys with a memorial begging forgiveness, and the Emperor issued an edict pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 河西王牧犍遣使上表，告嗣位。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hexi Mujian sent envoys to submit a memorial announcing his succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hexi Mujian sent envoys to submit a memorial announcing his succession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔以牧犍為都督涼、秦等四州諸軍事、征西大將軍、涼州刺史、河西王。

translations.literal: On wuyin, an edict appointed Mujian commander-in-chief of military affairs in Liang, Qin, and three other provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the West, inspector of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, an edict appointed Mujian commander-in-chief of military affairs in Liang, Qin, and three other provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the West, inspector of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiachen, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 燕王不遣太子質魏，散騎常侍劉滋諫曰：「昔劉禪有重山之險，孫皓有長江之阻，皆為晉擒。

translations.literal: The Yan king did not send his crown prince as hostage to Wei. Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Liu Zi remonstrated, saying: "In the past Liu Shan had the barrier of steep mountains and Sun Hao had the obstacle of the Yangtze—both were seized by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king did not send his crown prince as hostage to the Northern Wei. Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Liu Zi remonstrated, saying, "In the past Liu Shan had the barrier of steep mountains and Sun Hao had the Yangtze to shield him—yet both were taken by Jin.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 強弱之勢異也。

translations.literal: Because the balance of strength was different.
translations.idiomatic: Because the balance of strength was different.

sentences.zh: 今吾弱於吳、蜀而魏強於晉，不從其欲，將有危亡之禍。

translations.literal: Now we are weaker than Wu and Shu, while Wei is stronger than Jin was—if we do not yield to their demands, there will be the calamity of peril and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: We are weaker now than Wu and Shu were then, while Wei is stronger than Jin was. If we refuse what they demand, ruin will follow.

sentences.zh: 願亟遣太子，而修政事，撫百姓，收離散，賑饑窮，勸農桑，省賦役，社稷猶庶幾可保。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will swiftly send the crown prince, and meanwhile govern well, comfort the people, gather the scattered, relieve hunger and destitution, encourage farming and sericulture, reduce taxes and corvée, and then the altars of state may still perhaps be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send the crown prince at once, and meanwhile govern well: comfort the people, gather the scattered, relieve hunger and destitution, encourage farming and sericulture, and lighten taxes and corvée. Then the altars of state may yet be preserved."

sentences.zh: 燕王怒，殺之，辛亥，魏主遣撫軍大將軍永昌王健等伐燕，收其禾稼，徙民而還。

translations.literal: The Yan king in anger killed him. On xinhai, the Wei ruler dispatched the Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian, and others to attack Yan; they gathered up the grain crops, relocated the population, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king in anger had him killed. On xinhai, the Wei ruler dispatched Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Prince Yongchang Wang Jian and others to attack Yan. They harvested the grain, relocated the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬午，魏主如美稷，遂至隰城，命陽平王它督諸軍擊山胡白龍於西河。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu, the Wei ruler went to Meiji, then continued to Xicheng, and ordered Prince of Yangping Ta to direct the various armies in attacking the Shanhu chieftain Bai Long in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu, the Wei ruler went to Meiji and on to Xicheng, ordering Prince Yangping Ta to command the armies in attacking the Shanhu chieftain Bai Long in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 它，熙之子也。

translations.literal: Ta was the son of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Ta was the son of Xi.

sentences.zh: 魏主輕山胡，日引數十騎登山臨視之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler underestimated the Shanhu; daily he led several dozen horsemen up the mountain to look down upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler held the Shanhu in contempt and each day led several dozen horsemen up the mountain to look down on them.

sentences.zh: 白龍伏壯士十餘處掩擊之，魏主墜馬，幾為所擒。

translations.literal: Bai Long hid stalwart fighters in more than ten places and attacked by ambush; the Wei ruler fell from his horse and was nearly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Long hid stalwart fighters in more than ten places and struck from ambush. The Wei ruler was thrown from his horse and nearly taken.

sentences.zh: 內和行長代人陳建以身扞之，大呼奮擊，殺胡數人，身被十餘瘡，魏主乃免。

translations.literal: Neihe Xingzhang dairen Chen Jian shielded him with his body, cried out and fought fiercely, killed several Hu fighters, received more than ten wounds himself, and only then was the Wei ruler spared.
translations.idiomatic: Neihe Xingzhang dairen Chen Jian shielded him with his own body, shouting as he fought and killing several Hu fighters. Though he took more than a dozen wounds, the Wei ruler was spared.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊子，大破胡眾，斬白龍，屠其城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuzi, they routed the Hu forces, beheaded Bai Long, and slaughtered their city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuzi, they routed the Hu forces, beheaded Bai Long, and put his city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，魏人破白龍餘黨於五原，誅數千人，以其妻子賜將士。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu, the Wei army defeated Bai Long's remaining followers at Wuyuan, executed several thousand people, and gave their wives and children as rewards to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu, the Northern Wei defeated Bai Long's remaining followers at Wuyuan, executed several thousand people, and gave their wives and children to the officers and soldiers as rewards.

sentences.zh: 直一月，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: In the regular eleventh month, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，復如雲中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, he again went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, he again set out for Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之下元嘉十二年（

translations.literal: The lower part of "Emperor Wen of the Ancestor [dynasty], Part One" — Yuanjia year 12 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, Part One (continued) — Yuanjia year 12 (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元四三五年）

translations.literal: yihai, corresponding to 435 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yihai, corresponding to 435 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (jiwei), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (jiwei), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Emperor performed sacrifice at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 燕王數為魏所攻，遣使詣建康稱籓奉貢。

translations.literal: The Yan king, repeatedly attacked by Wei, sent envoys to Jiankang to profess vassalage and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly attacked by the Northern Wei, the Yan king sent envoys to Jiankang to profess vassalage and offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔封為燕王，江南謂之黃龍國。

translations.literal: On guiyou, an edict enfeoffed him as King of Yan; south of the Yangtze they called his state the Kingdom of Yellow Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, an edict enfeoffed him as King of Yan; south of the Yangtze his realm was called the Kingdom of Yellow Dragon.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏大赦，改元太延。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taiyan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taiyan.

sentences.zh: 有老父投書於敦煌東門，求之，不獲。

translations.literal: An old man cast a letter into the eastern gate of Dunhuang; when they searched for him, he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: An old man dropped a letter at the eastern gate of Dunhuang; when men searched for him, he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「涼王三十年若七年。」

translations.literal: The letter read: "The Prince of Liang—thirty years if [he acts thus], seven years if [otherwise]."
translations.idiomatic: The letter read, "The Prince of Liang—thirty years or seven."

sentences.zh: 河西王牧犍以問奉常張慎，對曰：「昔虢之將亡，神降於莘。

translations.literal: Prince of Hexi Mujian asked Chief Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Shen about it; Shen replied: "In olden days, when the state of Guo was about to perish, a deity descended at Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hexi Mujian asked Chief Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Shen about it. Shen replied, "In olden days, when the state of Guo was about to perish, a deity descended at Shen.

sentences.zh: 願殿下崇德修政，以享三十年之祚；

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will exalt virtue and reform government, thereby enjoying a reign of thirty years;
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Highness will exalt virtue and reform government, thereby enjoying a reign of thirty years;

sentences.zh: 若盤於游田，荒於酒色，臣恐七年將有大變。」

translations.literal: but if you indulge in hunting and are dissolute in wine and women, I fear that in seven years great upheaval will come."
translations.idiomatic: but if you indulge in hunting and are dissolute in wine and women, I fear that in seven years great upheaval will come."

sentences.zh: 牧犍不悅。

translations.literal: Mujian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian was displeased.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁未，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingwei, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingwei, the Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸亥，燕王遣大將湯燭入貢於魏，辭以太子王仁有疾，故未之遣。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guihai, the Yan king sent the general Tang Zhu to present tribute to Wei, excusing himself on the grounds that the crown prince Wang Ren was ill and therefore had not been sent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guihai, the Yan king sent the general Tang Zhu to present tribute to the Northern Wei, excusing himself on the grounds that Crown Prince Wang Ren was ill and therefore had not been sent.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍劉湛與僕射殷景仁素善，湛之入也，景仁實引之。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Army Liu Zhan and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yin Jingren had long been on good terms; when Zhan entered [court], Jingren had in fact been the one who recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Army Liu Zhan and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yin Jingren had long been on good terms; when Zhan entered court, Jingren had in fact recommended him.

sentences.zh: 湛既至，以景仁位遇本不逾己，而一旦居前，意甚憤憤；

translations.literal: Once Zhan had arrived, he felt that Jingren's rank and favor had originally not exceeded his own, yet Jingren had suddenly risen ahead of him, and he was deeply resentful;
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhan arrived, he felt that Jingren's rank and favor had originally been no greater than his own, yet Jingren had suddenly moved ahead of him, and he was deeply resentful;

sentences.zh: 俱被時遇，以景仁專管內任，謂為間己，猜隙漸生。

translations.literal: Both enjoyed imperial favor at the time; because Jingren alone managed inner-court duties, Zhan regarded this as coming between himself and the Emperor, and suspicion and rifts gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: Both enjoyed imperial favor, but because Jingren alone managed inner-court duties, Zhan took this as coming between himself and the Emperor, and suspicion and rifts gradually grew.

sentences.zh: 知帝信仗景仁，不可移奪，時司徒義康專秉朝權，湛嘗為義康上佐，遂委心自結，欲因宰相之力以回上意，傾黜景仁，獨當時務。

translations.literal: Knowing that the Emperor trusted and relied on Jingren and that this could not be changed, while at the time Minister over the Masses Yikang monopolized state power—and Zhan had once been Yikang's chief aide—he therefore pledged himself to Yikang wholeheartedly, hoping through the prime minister's power to turn the Emperor's mind, bring Jingren down, and hold court affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Emperor trusted Jingren and that this could not be changed, while Minister over the Masses Yikang then monopolized state power—and Zhan had once been Yikang's chief aide—Zhan pledged himself wholeheartedly to Yikang, hoping through the prime minister's power to turn the Emperor's mind, bring Jingren down, and hold court affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己巳，帝加景仁中書令、中護軍，即家為府；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, the Emperor additionally made Jingren Director of the Secretariat and Central Protector of the Army, establishing his residence as an office;
